roster.name: Ja'Marr Chase
roster.outlook: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals are set to host the 1-6 Titans in Week 8. He caught five of seven targets for 62 yards and a touchdown in Cincinnati's 35-13 Week 7 victory. Tee Higgins garnered the same number of looks from Joe Burrow, but Chase turned his into six receptions for 148 yards and a score. The good news is that the concussion appears to be behind Chase, and he'll be ready to exploit a Tennessee defense tied for 24th in fantasy points allowed per game (35.8) to WRs.

roster.name: Derrick Henry
roster.outlook: Derrick Henry and the Ravens aim to snap a two-game losing streak when they visit Buffalo in Week 8. He rushed 17 times for 45 yards and caught one of two targets for four yards during Baltimore's 35-13 loss in Week 7. Henry has averaged fewer than 3.5 yards per carry (YPC) in two straight outings, rushing 34 times for 103 yards (3.0 YPC) during that stretch. He'll look to turn things around versus a Bills defense allowing 28.0 fantasy points per game to RBs, which ranks 29th.

roster.name: Colston Loveland
roster.outlook: Colston Loveland will aim to continue producing as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Loveland stayed hot in a Week 7 win over New England, finishing with season highs in catches (7), targets (12), yards (69) and tacking on a touchdown. The second-year tight end has had a promising turnaround to the season, with 50 or more yards in three of his last four games and back-to-back outings with a score. He'll face a Seattle defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

roster.name: DJ Moore
roster.outlook: DJ Moore hopes to be fully healthy following Buffalo's bye week in advance of their Week 8 matchup with the Ravens. Moore hasn't played since a brief appearance in Week 4 due to a shoulder injury that has lingered since Week 2. When on the field, he has been Josh Allen's favorite target, collecting 18 looks in two games. Baltimore has allowed four 100-yard receivers and an attractive 9.3 yards per target, the fifth-highest in the league, making Moore an attractive option if he suits up.

roster.name: Rico Dowdle
roster.outlook: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers look to even the season series against the Browns in Week 8. He rushed nine times for 41 yards and caught all six of his targets for 45 yards in Week 7 during Pittsburgh's 16-10 victory in Paris. Dowdle finished first in receptions and second in yardage despite being out-touched by starter Jaylen Warren, who turned his 21 touches into 137 scrimmage yards. Dowdle was inactive for the Week 4 loss against Cleveland, so he'll look to make an impact with first place in the AFC North at stake.

roster.name: Aaron Jones Sr.
roster.outlook: Aaron Jones could be at risk of missing Week 8 as the Vikings travel to Detroit. Jones suffered a knee injury in Minnesota's Week 7 win over the Colts, and he's currently day-to-day. What this means for his status moving forward is unknown until practices start up this week, but it is promising that he avoided a significant injury. The veteran running back logged eight carries for 26 yards before his departure, and it appeared he was still holding a prominent role even with Jordan Mason back on the field. If Jones can get healthy, he'll face a Lions defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Kenyon Sadiq
roster.outlook: Kenyon Sadiq's role in the Jets' passing game is steadily declining ahead of their Week 8 matchup with the Raiders. After flashing in Week 3 with 105 yards on seven catches, Sadiq has totaled just four catches for 21 yards over the last four games, while Mason Taylor's stats continue to increase. While the Raiders have allowed the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends, it's almost all touchdown-related, surrendering eight in seven games but a low 6.5 yards per target average. With minimal volume, Sadiq's chances of reaching the end zone appear minimal.

roster.name: Trevor Lawrence
roster.outlook: Trevor Lawrence profiles as a strong Week 8 fantasy starter as the Jaguars return home to host the Colts following their Week 7 bye. In two previous starts at EverBank Stadium this season, Lawrence has thrown seven touchdown passes. He has a 14:4 TD:INT through six outings, the last two of which came in London. Back stateside, Lawrence should keep rolling at home against a Colts secondary that has allowed an 11:2 TD:INT and could remain without top CB Sauce Gardner (calf).

roster.name: Braelon Allen
roster.outlook: Braelon Allen's workload is unclear heading into the Jets' Week 8 matchup with the Raiders. He has shined over the last four games with Breece Hall (quad) sidelined, topping 100 total yards three times, but would likely be in a timeshare if Hall can return in Week 8. Both backs can still offer sound production as the matchup is one of the most favorable available. Las Vegas is surrendering 5.2 yards per carry and the second-most fantasy points per game, last week allowing two 90-plus yard rushers to the Rams.

roster.name: Malik Washington
roster.outlook: Malik Washington will hope for additional volume in Week 8 when the Dolphins host the Patriots. He collected a season-low three targets in Week 7, and volume has been the key to his fantasy relevance, having topped 56 yards once all season. It's a low-volume passing game that may be pressed into higher throw rates if Miami falls behind early, but Washington's role underneath doesn't create much upside despite facing a secondary that's surrendering a generous 8.8 yards per target.

roster.name: Jared Goff
roster.outlook: Jared Goff will aim to keep it rolling as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Goff's story stayed the same in a Week 7 win over the Packers, completing 22 of 32 passes for 303 yards and two touchdowns. The veteran quarterback has now passed for 300-plus yards in three of six games, and he's also dished out two or more touchdowns in all but one outing. He'll have his biggest test of the season this week, though, as Minnesota has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to the quarterback position.

roster.name: Germie Bernard
roster.outlook: Germie Bernard and the Steelers welcome the division-rival Browns to town in Week 8. The rookie caught three of five targets for 27 yards in Pittsburgh's 16-10 victory in Week 7 over the Saints in Paris. Bernard was relatively quiet after posting a 17-167-1 receiving line on 21 targets over his previous two outings. He'll look to bounce back versus a Cleveland defense tied for 19th in fantasy points allowed per game (32.4) to WRs.

roster.name: Josh Jacobs
roster.outlook: Josh Jacobs will look to ramp it up even more as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Jacobs carved out a solid performance in his return to the field against the Lions in Week 7, rushing the ball for 36 yards off 11 carries but catching five passes for 55 yards and a touchdown. While the rushing efficiency wasn't there, the usage definitely was, which bodes well for the veteran ball carrier. He could also be in store for a better outing on the ground, as Carolina has ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to RBs this campaign.

roster.name: Tyler Bass
roster.outlook: Tyler Bass has increased his workload over the last three weeks as Buffalo gets set to face Baltimore in Week 8. Always a steady source for PATs in Buffalo's high-scoring offense (Bass has made at least two in every game), he went from four field goals across his first three games to nine over his last three. None have come from 50-plus yards, potentially keeping bonus scoring off the table. Baltimore is a mid-tier defense for points allowed to kickers, but they've allowed as many field goal attempts as extra points through seven games, setting Bass up for a strong Week 8.

roster.name: Puka Nacua
roster.outlook: Puka Nacua will look to move further beyond a calf injury when the Rams face the Chargers in Week 8. Nacua played through the issue Sunday against Las Vegas and tallied eight catches on 10 targets for 68 yards and a touchdown while adding 10 yards on two carries. He logged an 85 percent offensive snap share, so he didn't seem to be inhibited by the calf injury. With Davante Adams (hamstring) expected to be sidelined several more games, Nacua should continue to see a lot of balls thrown his way against the Chargers, who have yielded a 68.9% catch rate to wideouts, third-worst in the league.

roster.name: Brock Bowers
roster.outlook: Brock Bowers has been held slightly in check the last two weeks, failing to see double-digit targets in either contest and managing a 10-143-0 line on 17 targets. Those are still strong numbers for a tight end, but a mild disappointment for an elite talent like Bowers. He remains the top option in the Raiders' passing game, even as No. 2 TE Michael Mayer continues to get more work than expected. Bowers will face a tough test in Week 8 against a Jets defense that ranks sixth in fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends, and which has given up just one TD to the position through seven games.

roster.name: Carnell Tate
roster.outlook: Carnell Tate has recorded at least 69 receiving yards in three of his last four games, establishing himself as a reliable fantasy option despite the ongoing struggles of Titans QB Cam Ward. Facing a Bengals defense that just allowed eight catches for 137 yards and a TD to top Ravens WR Zay Flowers, Tate is a high-end flex option for Week 8. The rookie fourth overall pick is averaging more than seven targets per game and could get plenty of opportunities if the 1-6 Titans fall behind as expected on the road against the 4-2 Bengals.

roster.name: Caleb Williams
roster.outlook: Caleb Williams will aim to stay hot as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Williams impressed in his second game back from a hamstring injury in Week 7, completing 67 percent of passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns over the Patriots. The third-year quarterback has now passed for 300-plus yards in back-to-back weeks, and he hasn't committed a turnover in that stretch. He'll take on a Seattle defense that's been tougher on QBs, ranking second in fantasy points allowed to the position.

roster.name: Tony Pollard
roster.outlook: Tony Pollard is coming off his best game of the season, as he racked up 129 rushing yards and three TDs against the Browns in Tennessee's Week 7 loss. The veteran RB is the most consistent offensive player on the Titans, having racked up at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in six consecutive games. His solid touch floor makes Pollard a passable fantasy RB2 for Week 8, but don't expect a repeat of his Week 7 outburst against a Bengals defense that has limited RBs to three total TDs in six games.

roster.name: Kyle Monangai
roster.outlook: Kyle Monangai will aim to make a return as the Bears travel to Seattle in Week 8. Monangai has missed the last three games with a turf toe injury, but Chicago is not planning to place him on IR. This makes it likely the second-year running back at least has a chance to return in the upcoming away tilt. With two 100-yard rushing games and three touchdowns across the first four games of the season, Monangai is an intriguing option if he returns, even against a Seahawks defense that's ranked top 10 in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

roster.name: J.K. Dobbins
roster.outlook: J.K. Dobbins may be in danger of losing his spot in the Broncos' offense. During a Week 7 win over the Cardinals, rookie Jonah Coleman led the backfield with nine carries compared to Dobbins' six, and Coleman's 11 touches were also more than RJ Harvey's five. Both Dobbins and Harvey got into the end zone while Coleman didn't, suggesting that this could be turning into a full-blown committee. Dobbins doesn't contribute as a pass catcher the way Harvey does, so if he gets supplanted on early downs by Coleman, he may fade out of the game plan entirely. Dobbins will have trouble producing on limited volume in Week 8 versus a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Isiah Pacheco
roster.outlook: Isiah Pacheco will stay sidelined in Week 8 as the Lions take on Minnesota. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return this season in jeopardy. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will continue to handle RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.

roster.name: Tyler Loop
roster.outlook: Tyler Loop and the Ravens visit the 5-1 Bills in Week 8. He connected on both of his field-goal attempts and his lone PAT during Baltimore's 35-13 loss in Week 7. Following a 30-point outing in an overtime victory in Week 5, the Ravens' offense has struggled mightily over the last two games, combining for just 23 points over that stretch. However, with Lamar Jackson (ankle) progressing toward a return from a three-game absence, Loop could have more opportunities to score versus a Bills defense allowing 28.5 points per contest, the third-most in the NFL.

roster.name: Kyler Murray
roster.outlook: Kyler Murray will look to do more as the Vikings play the Lions in Week 8. Murray completed 14 of 24 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown, with five carries for 39 yards in a Week 7 win over the Colts. The veteran has yet to lose a game this year, but his output has been quite low compared to that of usual winning quarterbacks. He'll luckily face a Detroit defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game to QBs so far this season.

roster.name: Ollie Gordon II
roster.outlook: Ollie Gordon may be hindered by an unfavorable game flow in Week 8 when the Dolphins host the Patriots. He has scored in four straight games, topping 100 yards twice while amassing at least 17 carries three times. Jaylen Wright is uncertain to play in Week 8, which could result in 20-plus carries for Miami's only option in the backfield if they remain competitive and aren't forced to throw the entire second half. New England brings a mid-tier run defense into Week 8, allowing 4.1 yards per carry but just five rushing scores in seven games.

roster.name: Kalif Raymond
roster.outlook: Kalif Raymond figures to be a depth option once again as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Raymond logged his first catch-less game of the season in Week 7, which only supports the fact that his role has diminished at this point in the year. The veteran pass catcher remains a safe option in the passing game, but he's way behind Rome Odunze and Luther Burden in the wide receiver hierarchy. Seattle has ranked first in fantasy points allowed to WRs so far this season.

roster.name: Breece Hall
roster.outlook: Breece Hall's role is uncertain if he returns from a quad injury in Week 8 when the Jets face the Raiders. Hall has not played since Week 3 and has topped 32 yards just once, while Braelon Allen has shined during his absence. Being eased back into action appears more likely than immediately commanding the Jets' backfield, but he may not require heavy volume to be an intriguing asset, as the Raiders are allowing the second-most fantasy points per game to opposing running backs and 5.2 yards per carry. Five opposing backs have rushed for 94 yards or more against them.

roster.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
roster.outlook: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns visit the Steelers for an AFC North battle in Week 8. He brought in six of nine targets for 91 yards and also lost a fumble during Cleveland's 27-24 Week 7 win. Fannin finished second behind KC Concepcion (8-129-0 on 10 targets) in receptions, yardage, and targets while setting a new season high in receiving yards. Fannin will look to exploit the Pittsburgh defense again after he recorded a 3-27-1 line against them in a Week 4 victory.

roster.name: Dak Prescott
roster.outlook: Dak Prescott tossed multiple touchdowns last game for Dallas for the first time since the middle of September. Prescott threw for 212 yards and three touchdowns in the 38-21 win over the Eagles. Prescott now has 13 touchdowns in seven starts in 2026. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL. The Cardinals have also given up the most points per game in the NFL overall to date.

roster.name: Tre Tucker
roster.outlook: Tre Tucker is on his way to a career-best season with Kirk Cousins under center for the Raiders. The fourth-year wideout has caught 10 of 19 targets for 200 yards and three touchdowns over the last two games, and through seven contests Tucker sports a 29-474-4 line on 47 targets. Brock Bowers is still the team's top downfield threat, but Tucker is establishing himself as a strong No. 2 option, although the eventual switch at QB to rookie Fernando Mendoza could change things. Tucker will look to keep rolling in Week 8 against a Jets secondary that is tied for 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Jaylen Warren
roster.outlook: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers host the Browns for a Week 8 divisional clash. He had 18 carries for 101 yards and corralled three of four targets for 36 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 7 victory in Paris. Fellow running back Rico Dowdle amassed 86 scrimmage yards on 15 touches, and it appears he's rounding into form after missing nearly a month with a toe injury. Warren remains atop the backfield hierarchy, but he'll face a tough test against Cleveland's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to RBs.

roster.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
roster.outlook: Ja'Kobi Lane and the Ravens are in Buffalo for a Week 8 showdown. The rookie corralled three of five targets for 25 yards during Baltimore's 35-13 Week 7 defeat. Lane tied for second on the team in receptions and finished second behind Zay Flowers' 11 looks from Tyler Huntley. Lamar Jackson (ankle) has a decent chance to return against Buffalo's 32nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (42.3) to WRs, but Lane is still an unproven fantasy commodity on an offense that prefers to run the ball.

roster.name: Omar Cooper Jr.
roster.outlook: Omar Cooper's two-week surge is set to extend into Week 8 when the Jets have an inviting matchup with the Raiders. Cooper has topped 100 yards and scored in consecutive outings since returning from an ankle injury, while snagging 11 of his 12 targets. The volume remains modest in a run-first offense, but Las Vegas is allowing 8.9 yards per target to opposing wide receivers with seven similar players registering at least 53 receiving yards.

roster.name: Garrett Wilson
roster.outlook: Garrett Wilson's high-volume role has faded over the last two weeks as the Jets prepare to host the Raiders in Week 8. After recording 57 or more yards in four of his first five games, Wilson has just 70 total yards over the last two weeks, coinciding with Omar Cooper's emergence. While the Raiders are allowing 8.9 yards per target to opposing wideouts, smaller, shifty receivers have given them fits (DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, Xavier Worthy), suggesting Wilson carries ample volatility into Week 8.

roster.name: Chase McLaughlin
roster.outlook: Chase McLaughlin could have few scoring opportunities in the Buccaneers' Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. McLaughlin converted on all seven of his kicks in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, making two field goals and five extra points. On the season, McLaughlin has been perfect, making all 16 of his field-goal tries and all 16 of his point-after attempts. Despite this, McLaughlin could struggle against a solid Falcons defense that's allowed just 6.4 kicking points per game this season.

roster.name: Caleb Douglas
roster.outlook: Caleb Douglas appears to be emerging as a big-play option in the Dolphins' low-volume passing game ahead of a Week 8 matchup with the Patriots. Returning from a three-game absence in Week 7, Douglas brought in two of three targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns. He's only caught two balls in two of his three healthy appearances, but is averaging 20.3 yards per catch, and his large frame makes him a potential red zone candidate. If New England jumps out to an early lead, it could help Douglas' snap share, setting him up as a low-floor, high-ceiling option against a defense allowing a generous 8.8 yards per target.

roster.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
roster.outlook: Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues to look like an unstoppable force for Seattle with a Week 8 matchup against the Bears on tap. Smith-Njigba caught nine of 12 targets for 150 yards and a touchdown against Kansas City this past Sunday, marking his sixth performance of 100-plus receiving yards through seven weeks. The budding superstar leads the NFL with 867 receiving yards and eight receiving touchdowns through seven weeks. He'll next face a Chicago defense that ranks 30th in the NFL with 9.51 yards per target yielded to wide receivers.

roster.name: Bucky Irving
roster.outlook: Bucky Irving will look to stay hot in the Buccaneers' Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Irving carried the load for Tampa Bay's offense in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, rushing for 106 and two touchdowns while catching one of two targets for four yards. Irving has been the focal point of the Buccaneers' offense over the last three weeks, averaging 111.3 total yards and 1.3 touchdowns per game during that span. He's in for a very favorable Week 8 matchup as well, with Atlanta's defense allowing 26.8 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.

roster.name: Luther Burden III
roster.outlook: Luther Burden will look to build off a season-best performance as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Burden was on fire in Week 7 against the Patriots, turning four catches into 130 yards and a touchdown and taking his one carry for seven yards. The second-year pass catcher has now totaled 35 receptions for 491 yards and two touchdowns this season, and he's becoming Caleb Williams' favorite option in the passing game. Burden will now shift focus to a tough Seattle defense that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

roster.name: Courtland Sutton
roster.outlook: Courtland Sutton had another quiet day in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, managing to catch three of five targets for 45 yards. The veteran wideout has been held under 50 receiving yards and three catches or fewer in all seven games so far this season, and he's scored just one TD after hauling in 25 over the prior three years. Sutton isn't likely to break out in Week 8 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Matthew Golden
roster.outlook: Matthew Golden will look to bounce back as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Golden wasn't abysmal in a Week 7 loss to the Lions, but he logged a season-low 39 yards on six catches. The second-year pass catcher has still totaled 36 grabs for 540 yards and three touchdowns across the seven games of the season, completely obliterating his 39-361-0 receiving line from the 2025 season across 14 games. He'll face a Carolina defense that's ranked a tough fifth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

roster.name: Travis Kelce
roster.outlook: Travis Kelce made history again in Week 7, moving into fifth place on the NFL's all-time reception list with 1,104 as Kansas City fell to the Seahawks. The veteran tight end remains Patrick Mahomes' most reliable pass catcher, and through six games, Kelce's delivered a 24-343-2 line on 35 targets. The 37-year-old is no longer as dangerous with the ball in his hands, but he can still move the chains consistently. Kelce will take on a Broncos defense in Week 8 that ranks 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Cairo Santos
roster.outlook: Cairo Santos will look to stay busy as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Santos went 3-for-4 on field-goal attempts, including a career-high 58-yarder, and nailed all three of his XPAs in a Week 7 win over the Patriots. The veteran has now missed a field-goal try in each of the last three weeks,  but he's gone an otherwise serviceable 11-for-15 on field goals, and 21-for-21 on extra-point kicks this season. He'll face a Seattle squad that's ranked sixth in fantasy points allowed to kickers.

roster.name: MarShawn Lloyd
roster.outlook: MarShawn Lloyd figures to be a complementary option once again as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Lloyd's role wasn't completely chalked with the return of Josh Jacobs in Week 7, as he still logged six carries for 20 yards and caught two passes for 15 yards. Jacobs also averaged just 3.27 yards per carry on the ground, which could keep Lloyd relevant as a secondary rushing option if this persists. Carolina has ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this season, so Lloyd will aim to take advantage of what could be limited touches.

roster.name: Pat Freiermuth
roster.outlook: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers return home to host the Browns for an AFC North showdown in Week 8. He caught two of four targets for 20 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 7 win in Paris. Freiermuth played 34 offensive snaps to fellow TE Darnell Washington's 36, but the two have been essentially neck-and-neck in playing time through seven outings this season. Freiermuth will aim to stand out versus Cleveland's 20th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (13.9) to the position.

roster.name: Makai Lemon
roster.outlook: Makai Lemon set career highs across the board last game for the Eagles. With both DeVonta Smith as well as Dontayvion Wicks sidelined due to injury, Lemon snagged seven passes for 67 yards and his first NFL touchdown. He was targeted eight times in the contest. If Smith and/or Wicks are unable to suit up in Week 8 versus the Commanders, Lemon could have a delicious matchup, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.

roster.name: Chase Brown
roster.outlook: Chase Brown and the Bengals welcome the Titans to town for a Week 8 showdown. He rushed 11 times for 39 yards and caught four of five targets for 19 yards during Cincinnati's 35-13 victory in Week 7. Over his last three outings, Brown has 33 carries for 88 yards (2.7 yards per carry). He'll look to bounce back against a Tennessee defense that gave up 183 rushing yards and three total TDs to the Browns in Week 7.

roster.name: Geno Smith
roster.outlook: Geno Smith is poised to build on one of his best outings of the year when the Jets host the Raiders in Week 8. He threw for three touchdowns in Week 7 against Miami, his second game in seven outings at that mark, while the other five have produced just one touchdown or none. Las Vegas has allowed multiple touchdowns in five straight games and 16 scores overall, the second-highest total across the league. Smith needs to find paydirt to be a viable option, as the Raiders have surrendered more than 255 passing yards just once.

roster.name: Trey Smack
roster.outlook: Trey Smack will need to get back on track as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Smack had another rough outing in Week 7 against the Vikings, making two PATs but going just 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts. The rookie has now missed five field goals and two extra-point tries this season, and his job will definitely be in jeopardy if he continues to be inaccurate. He'll face a Carolina squad that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy kickers this season.

roster.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
roster.outlook: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to get back in the end zone as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Gibbs hit the century mark on the ground for the third time this season in Week 7 versus Green Bay, rushing the ball 29 times for 116 yards and adding five catches for 27 yards. The superstar unfortunately was held to zero touchdowns for the first time this season, with nine to his name across the first five games. He'll change focus now to a Minnesota defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

roster.name: A.J. Brown
roster.outlook: A.J. Brown will look to get on track when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. Brown has caught three passes in each of his three outings for his new squad, failing to score or top 48 receiving yards. While Miami has surrendered 14 touchdown passes overall, only three have gone to wide receivers, resulting in the second-fewest fantasy points allowed despite an appealing 8.8 yards per target. Brown may still be a week away from a breakout in his new uniform.

roster.name: Tetairoa McMillan
roster.outlook: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top wideout in the Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Despite Carolina's offensive struggles in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, McMillan was relatively productive, catching four of six targets for 40 yards. On the season, the second-year pro has nabbed 36 of 54 targets for 511 yards (11th-most in the NFL) and two touchdowns in just six contests. He could find success in Week 8 against a Packers secondary that's given up six receiving touchdowns to opposing WRs this season.

roster.name: Rome Odunze
roster.outlook: Rome Odunze will look to capitalize on his opportunities as the Bears travel to Seattle in Week 8. Odunze was outperformed by teammate Luther Burden once again in Week 7 against the Patriots, logging four catches for 69 yards to Burden's four catches for 130 yards and a touchdown. Odunze has still been solid throughout this year, with a 24-381-0 receiving line over the first seven games of the season. He'll face a Seahawks defense that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Lamar Jackson
roster.outlook: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens visit the Bills in Week 8. After missing the last three contests with an ankle injury, he appears to be headed in the right direction, as head coach Jesse Minter stated Jackson is "in a decent spot" to return to action against Buffalo. His practice participation bears monitoring following his limited activity prior to Baltimore's Week 7 loss. If active, Jackson will aim to snap a two-game losing streak versus a Bills defense allowing 26.5 fantasy points per game (30th) to QBs.

roster.name: Chuba Hubbard
roster.outlook: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Hubbard had his worst performance of the season in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, accumulating just 60 yards on 11 touches. Across six contests this season, Hubbard has amassed 459 rushing yards, 112 receiving yards and six total touchdown, the 19th-most total yards in the NFL. He'll have a good opportunity to rebound in Week 8 against a Packers defense that's allowed 25.8 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.

roster.name: Brian Thomas Jr.
roster.outlook: Brian Thomas has dropped out of fantasy starting consideration in virtually all formats after finishing without a reception in each of Jacksonville's last two games. He has been outplayed by Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers throughout the season, and even Josh Cameron and Travis Hunter have found more success in recent weeks than Thomas among Jacksonville's wide receivers. Thomas will face a Colts defense in Week 8 that's giving up 142 yards per game to WRs, but don't expect him to be a significant contributor considering he has been limited to a 9-105-1 receiving line on 20 targets through six games.

roster.name: Mark Andrews
roster.outlook: Mark Andrews and the Ravens travel to face the Bills in Week 8. He caught three of four targets for 23 yards during Baltimore's 35-13 defeat in Week 7. Andrews was unable to take advantage of game flow, as Tyler Huntley attempted 34 passes and threw for a career-high 298 yards. Andrews has failed to top 30 receiving yards in five straight outings, making him a tough start in fantasy despite the potential return of Lamar Jackson (ankle).

roster.name: Xavier Worthy
roster.outlook: Xavier Worthy struggled in Week 7 while filling in as Kansas City's No. 1 wide receiver, catching just three of six targets for 11 yards in a loss to the Seahawks. The third-year speedster has yet to reach 80 receiving yards this season, and it's looking increasingly like he won't live up to the billing of being the 28th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. Once Rashee Rice is cleared to return from a hamstring strain, Worthy might benefit from returning to a more comfortable supporting role. He'll try to bounce back in Week 8 against a Broncos secondary that could again be without Pat Surtain, but still ranks sixth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Bryce Young
roster.outlook: Bryce Young will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Panthers' Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Young underwhelmed for the first time all season in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, completing 14 of 27 passes for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Despite this, Young has been one of the league's most productive quarterbacks this season, throwing for an average of 285.3 yards and 2.0 touchdowns per game. He'll look to rebound in Week 8 against a strong Packers defense that's given up just 17.8 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.

roster.name: Will Reichard
roster.outlook: Will Reichard should remain a high-usage option as the Vikings play the Lions in Week 8. Reichard stayed busy in Week 7 against the Colts, but he did miss his first kick of the season going 3-for-4 on field-goal attempts. Even so, the third-year boot has now gone 18-for-19 on field-goal tries, including six makes from 50-plus yards, and nailed all nine of his XPAs this season. Detroit has ranked a tough third in fantasy points allowed to kickers.

roster.name: Kenny Gainwell
roster.outlook: Kenny Gainwell is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Gainwell had his most productive outing of the 2026 campaign in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, rushing 14 times for 88 yards. Despite his productive day, Gainwell still tallied 10 fewer carries than Bucky Irving (24 rushes for 106 yards and two touchdowns), suggesting he remains firmly behind Irving in Tampa Bay's backfield. However, Gainwell could remain successful in Week 8 against a Falcons defense that's given up 10 total touchdowns to running backs this season.

roster.name: Antonio Williams
roster.outlook: Antonio Williams should see an uptick in targets for the remainder of the season, as No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign for the Commanders due to a knee injury. Williams has double-digit catches in every game thus far during his rookie year, and should slot in just behind Stefon Diggs in terms of opportunities in the passing game moving forward. Following the bye, Washington will face division rival Philadelphia in Week 8. The reeling Eagles have been suspect in defending the pass this season.  Philadelphia is giving up 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.

roster.name: Chig Okonkwo
roster.outlook: Chig Okonkwo has posted back-to-back 60-plus yard outings for Washington, and could see an uptick in targets for the remainder of the season.  No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign for the Commanders due to a knee injury. Okonkwo has amassed 13 targets in the last two games alone. In Week 8, Washington will face division rival Philadelphia. The reeling Eagles have been suspect in defending the pass this season. Philadelphia is giving up 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.

roster.name: Jonathan Taylor
roster.outlook: Jonathan Taylor has at least 92 rushing yards and a TD in five of the Colts' seven games, keeping him firmly in set-and-forget fantasy RB1 territory for Week 8 despite a difficult matchup against Jacksonville's elite front. The Jaguars are allowing a league-low 72 rushing yards per game and boast the league's third-best scoring defense at 17.3 points per game. Taylor has handled 20-plus touches in all but one game this season and should remain busy in Week 8, as long as the 2-5 Colts stay within striking distance of the 4-2 Jaguars.

roster.name: Trey McBride
roster.outlook: Trey McBride has established himself as one of the NFL's top pass catchers ahead of Arizona's Week 8 matchup in Dallas. The star tight end posted season-best marks with 10 catches and 111 yards while scoring his fourth touchdown in Week 7 against Denver. McBride leads the NFL with 59 catches on the campaign, and he's tied for second with 78 targets. The Cowboys rank middle-of-the-pack against tight ends this season, but McBride is as matchup-proof as any player at his position in the league.

roster.name: DeVonta Smith
roster.outlook: DeVonta Smith missed Philadelphia's last game after aggravating a hamstring injury. Smith has played in just four games this season due to the nagging issue, which could also leave him sidelined in Week 8 versus the Commanders. If he is able to suit up, Smith could have a tasty matchup, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.

roster.name: Bhayshul Tuten
roster.outlook: Bhayshul Tuten scored two receiving TDs against the Texans in Jacksonville's last action prior to a Week 7 bye. The well-rested lead back is a high-end fantasy RB2 for his return to action in Week 8 against the Colts, who are allowing 134 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Tuten is averaging 86 scrimmage yards on 18 touches per game and has scored four total TDs through six outings. His well-rounded skill set gives him a high touch floor regardless of how the game unfolds.

roster.name: Matthew Stafford
roster.outlook: Matthew Stafford continues to put up prolific numbers for the Rams heading into a Week 8 matchup versus the Chargers. The reigning NFL MVP threw for 195 yards and three touchdowns against Las Vegas in Week 7, though he also tossed his seventh interception. Stafford has now compiled over 300 passing yards and/or multiple passing touchdowns in all but one game so far this season, and he leads the league with 1,989 total passing yards. The Chargers could at least offer some resistance, as they've allowed a modest 18.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season, ninth-best in the league.

roster.name: Parker Washington
roster.outlook: Parker Washington leads the Jaguars with a 26-416-4 receiving line on 46 targets through the Week 7 bye, and he has a nice opportunity to add to his team-best receiving totals in Week 8 against a Colts defense that may remain without top CB Sauce Gardner (calf) for a second consecutive game. Indianapolis ranks in the middle of the pack against WRs, allowing 142 yards per game to the position, though the Colts give up 25.7 points per game overall, ranking among the league's 10 most generous scoring defenses. Washington is on the fantasy WR1/WR2 borderline for this Week 8 home game.

roster.name: Jalen Coker
roster.outlook: Jalen Coker (shoulder) is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's top targets if active for Carolina's Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Coker underwhelmed in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, catching just one of four targets for nine yards, his least productive game since Week 7 of 2025. Coker has been one of the league's best wideouts when healthy this season, averaging 5.8 receptions and 77.5 yards per game in his four full games in 2026. If active for Week 8, he could have plenty of scoring opportunities against a Packers secondary that's allowed 35.4 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

roster.name: Emanuel Wilson
roster.outlook: Emanuel Wilson's role for Week 8 against the Bears could depend on whether Zach Charbonnet (knee) and/or Jadarian Price (chest) is ready to rejoin Seattle's backfield. As the Seahawks' lead RB in Week 7 against Kansas City, Wilson racked up 100 yards and a touchdown on a hearty 24 carries and added one catch for 15 yards. It was the third time over his past four contests that Wilson logged 20 or more totes, but should Charbonnet and/or Price be ready to return to the fold, Wilson will likely handle a reduced workload. Either way, he could find room to run against a Chicago defense that ranks 25th in the league with 4.33 yards per carry allowed to running backs.

roster.name: Dontayvion Wicks
roster.outlook: Dontayvion Wicks missed Philadelphia's last game due to an ankle injury. It was the first missed game of the season for Wicks, though he could also be sidelined in Week 8 versus the Commanders. If he is able to suit up, Wicks could have a delectable matchup, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.

roster.name: George Pickens
roster.outlook: George Pickens found the end zone last game for Dallas. Pickens snagged four passes for 57 yards and the touchdown. It was his second score in three outings. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL.

roster.name: Seth McGowan
roster.outlook: Seth McGowan set career highs with 48 scrimmage yards on 12 touches in the Colts' Week 7 loss to Minnesota, but the rookie seventh-round pick has yet to score a TD and is averaging a meager 21 scrimmage yards per game as Jonathan Taylor's backup. McGowan has become a popular fantasy waiver target as the possibility of Taylor being traded comes into focus, but McGowan is nothing more than a speculative bench stash as long as Taylor stays put and is healthy. The rookie's standalone appeal for Week 8 is minimal against a league-best Jaguars run defense that's yielding just 72 yards per game on the ground.

roster.name: CeeDee Lamb
roster.outlook: CeeDee Lamb scored twice last game for the Cowboys.  Lamb led the Cowboys receivers in all categories, snagging five passes for 74 yards and the two touchdowns. He has found the end zone six times in seven contests. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL.

roster.name: Kenneth Walker III
roster.outlook: Kenneth Walker was on the receiving end of a revenge game by the Seahawks' defense in Week 7, getting held to a season-low 36 rushing yards and zero TDs. Last season's Super Bowl MVP is still second in the NFL in rushing yards with 701, just three behind Bijan Robinson, and Walker has played one fewer game thanks to Kansas City's early Week 5 bye. Walker will try to stay on course for the 2026 rushing crown in Week 8 against a Broncos defense that ranks 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Jaylen Waddle
roster.outlook: Jaylen Waddle left the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals in the fourth quarter with a chest injury after producing a modest 4-48-0 line on seven targets. The former Miami wideout hasn't been able to get comfortable in his new environment; he has been held under 50 receiving yards in six of his first seven games for Denver. The severity of Waddle's injury isn't clear, but the team had little incentive to get him back on the field with a big lead. Assuming he is cleared to play in Week 8, he'll have a tough time producing a ceiling game against a Kansas City secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Jayden Daniels
roster.outlook: Jayden Daniels produced one of his best games of the season before the bye for the Commanders, and will look to build off of that performance in Week 8 versus the Eagles.  Daniels completed 72.5-percent of his passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns in a narrow loss to the 49ers. In fact, it was the first time in 2026 that Daniels threw for even 200 yards in a contest. Daniels will face an Eagles defense that has been better against the run than the pass this season.  Philadelphia is allowing 244.5 passing yards per contest, which is 27th in the NFL.  However, Philadelphia is still surrendering 119.3 yards per game on the ground, which is just 21st in the league.

roster.name: Christian Watson
roster.outlook: Christian Watson will aim to return to dominance as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Watson brought in five of eight targets for a team-leading 57 yards in a Week 7 loss to the Lions, which was his lowest yardage total since Week 4. The wideout still has a 34-595-6 receiving line through the first seven games of the season, and he's not far off from outpacing his stat totals from the 2024 and 2025 season. Carolina has ranked a stern fifth in fantasy points allowed to WRs this campaign.

roster.name: Dallas Goedert
roster.outlook: Dallas Goedert finished second on the Eagles last game in receptions, receiving yards and targets. Goedert caught five passes on seven looks for 48 yards in the 38-21 loss to the Cowboys. Goedert has at least seven targets in three-straight outings. If DeVonta Smith and/or Dontayvion Wicks are unable to suit up in Week 8 versus the Commanders, Goedert should remain a focal point of the passing attack, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.

roster.name: AJ Barner
roster.outlook: AJ Barner should continue to lead Seattle's tight-end corps in Week 8 against the Bears. In Week 7 versus Kansas City, Barner recorded his second-most catches (four) and receiving yards (42) in a contest this season. Though he's yet to get into the end zone and isn't putting up prolific numbers, Barner has logged an offensive snap count of at least 80% in each of the Seahawks seven games. Chicago ranks 17th in the NFL by giving up 8.3fantasy points per game to tight ends.

roster.name: Spencer Shrader
roster.outlook: Spencer Shrader leads the league in field goals made (19) and attempted (21), but he was just 1-for-3 in the Week 7 loss to Minnesota after starting 18-for-18 through six games. The Colts' kicker will attempt to bounce back in Week 8 against the Jaguars, who boast the league's third-stingiest scoring defense, allowing just 17.3 points per game. Shrader has earned some goodwill from fantasy managers with his hot start, but he could find himself back on the waiver wire before long if the misses start to pile up.

roster.name: Tyler Allgeier
roster.outlook: Tyler Allgeier's role in Arizona's background is looking shaky ahead of a Week 8 battle in Dallas. Rookie Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is expected to practice this week and could return from a two-game absence, which would likely push Allgeier down in the pecking order. Even if Love doesn't return, Bam Knight has outperformed Allgeier during Love's absence and could take over the lead-back role. Still, Allgeier at least has a good matchup, as the Cowboys rank 25th in the league in giving up 4.36 yards per carry to running backs.

roster.name: Keaton Mitchell
roster.outlook: Keaton Mitchell's usage declined in Week 6, prior to the Chargers' bye. After averaging nearly 12 touches per game in the preceding two weeks, Mitchell had two carries for just four yards, while Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal handled bigger workloads. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is scrambling to find answers, so Mitchell is expected to get more chances to prove he deserves a consistent role. However, so far in 2026, he hasn't produced more than 52 rushing yards or 63 scrimmage yards in a game. In Week 8, he will take on a Rams defense that is tied for 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Ashton Jeanty
roster.outlook: Ashton Jeanty continues to struggle on the ground while making an impact as a pass catcher. In the Raiders' Week 7 loss to the Rams, the second-year player gained a season-low 15 rushing yards on eight carries, but caught all eight of his targets for 61 yards and a touchdown. Jeanty has gotten at least six targets in six of seven games so far in 2026, turning that volume into a 34-312-3 line on 44 looks. but his 3.1 yards per carry suggests he simply isn't cut out to be a No. 1 back. He'll try to bring some balance to his stat line in Week 8 against a Jets defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Zay Flowers
roster.outlook: Zay Flowers and the Ravens look to halt a two-game losing skid when they visit the Bills in Week 8. He caught eight of 11 targets for 137 yards and a touchdown in Baltimore's 35-13 Week 7 defeat. Flowers led the team in receptions, yardage, and targets by a wide margin, recording the Ravens' only touchdown in the loss. There's a good chance Lamar Jackson (ankle) will return from a three-game absence in Week 8, but Flowers has proven to be a fantasy stud this season no matter who's under center. He'll face a Buffalo defense that surrenders 42.3 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs, the most in the league.

roster.name: Tee Higgins
roster.outlook: Tee Higgins and the Bengals return home for an AFC showdown against the Titans in Week 8. He caught six of seven targets for 148 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 35-13 win in Week 7. Higgins tied with Ja'Marr Chase (5-62-1) in targets but paced the Bengals in receptions and yardage for the second time in three contests. Higgins will aim to keep rolling against a Titans defense allowing 35.8 fantasy points per game to WRs, which is tied for 24th.

roster.name: TreVeyon Henderson
roster.outlook: TreVeyon Henderson's declining role in the Patriots' rushing approach leads to low expectations in a Week 8 matchup against the Dolphins. He has logged single-digit carries in three straight games and sits with a 3.9 yards per carry average after a 5.1 mark as a rookie. He's also only caught four passes, an area where Miami has been particularly vulnerable against running backs. With New England seemingly happy to distribute the workload across multiple players, an uptick in usage for Henderson appears unlikely.

roster.name: Joe Burrow
roster.outlook: Joe Burrow and the Bengals return home to host the 1-6 Titans in Week 8. He completed 22 of 30 pass attempts for 292 yards with four touchdowns and zero interceptions and rushed twice for 12 yards during Cincinnati's 35-13 victory in Week 7. It was Burrow's second straight outing with four TDs and no INTs, as he threw all of his scores in the second half. Up next is a Tennessee defense allowing 19.2 fantasy points per game to QBs, which ranks 12th.

roster.name: Michael Wilson
roster.outlook: Michael Wilson will look to get back his early-season mojo with a juicy matchup when Arizona faces the Cowboys in Week 8. After hauling in 18 passes on 30 targets for 184  yards across Weeks 3 and 4, Wilson has compiled just 12 receptions on 22 targets for 117 yards over his past three games. The downturn has some in spite of the Cardinals trading away Marvin Harrison to make Wilson the team's clear-cut No. 1 wide receiver, though tight end Trey McBride has continued to feature as QB Jacoby Brissett's top target. Harrison will have a chance to put up big numbers versus a Dallas defense that ranks 27th in the NFL with 23.9 fantasy points per game allowed to wideouts.

roster.name: RJ Harvey
roster.outlook: RJ Harvey logged just five touches in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, but he turned one of them into a 52-yard TD reception in the third quarter to salvage his day. The second-year back finished third in the backfield in workload behind rookie Jonah Coleman (11 touches) and veteran J.K. Dobbins (six touches), but Harvey seems to have a steady role as a passing-down option for Bo Nix. Even if Sean Payton continues to roll with a committee approach to his ground game, Harvey's floor should be relatively secure, even if his ceiling is limited to occasional big plays. He's unlikely to make a splash in Week 8 against a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Khalil Shakir
roster.outlook: Khalil Shakir will reprise his slot role in Week 8 when the Bills host the Ravens. Shakir hasn't directly benefited from DJ Moore's (shoulder) absence, with a largely unchanged role prior to Buffalo's Week 7 bye, logging six or more targets in four of six contests. While he's topped four catches just once, he's averaging 13.2 yards per catch, his highest mark since 2023. Baltimore's secondary has been more vulnerable to larger, outside X receivers, with Drake London, Tee Higgins, and Carnell Tate all topping 100 yards against them. Shakir will need to continue to take advantage of his opportunities to be a viable fantasy option.

roster.name: Jerry Jeudy
roster.outlook: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns take on the Steelers for a Week 8 road tilt. He caught all four of his targets for 21 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 comeback victory in Week 7. The outing marked two straight with at least four receptions for Jeudy, although he's still clearly behind rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston, and tight end Harold Fannin Jr. in the passing game. Jeudy remains off the fantasy radar in this AFC North showdown.

roster.name: Jake Bates
roster.outlook: Jake Bates will aim to stay perfect as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Bates nailed both of his two extra-point tries and two field-goal attempts including a game winner in Week 7 against the Packers. The third-year kicker has yet to miss a kick this season, making 10 field goals and 22 XPAs. He'll face a Minnesota team that's ranked fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to kickers (5.3).

roster.name: Darius Cooper
roster.outlook: Darius Cooper disappointed for Philadelphia last game despite the Eagles dealing with a multitude of injuries at the wide receiver position. Both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks were sidelined due to injury, but Cooper still only managed just one catch for 17 yards. He was targeted eight times in the contest, though rookie Makai Lemon saw eight targets by contrast. If Smith and/or Wicks are unable to suit up in Week 8 versus the Commanders, the matchup still favors Cooper, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.

roster.name: Chris Boswell
roster.outlook: Chris Boswell and the Steelers play host to the division rival Browns in Week 8. He went 3-for-3 on field goals and converted his lone PAT during Pittsburgh's 16-10 victory over the Saints in Paris. Boswell is looking to avenge his underwhelming performance against Cleveland in Week 4, as the 35-year-old missed one of two FGAs in the 27-24 defeat. Since then, Boswell is 9-for-10 on FGs and 7-for-7 on extra points. He'll try to keep rolling versus a Browns defense allowing 20.9 points per game, the 12th-fewest in the league.

roster.name: Hunter Henry
roster.outlook: Hunter Henry is poised to build on a season-high performance in Week 7 when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. While he failed to reach the end zone for the first time in three games, Henry hauled in all seven of his targets for 71 yards, all season bests. Miami has been exploited by opposing tight ends with six touchdown receptions in six games and 9.3 yards per target, the second highest mark in the league. New England continues to spread targets around, but it seems wise to scheme into this vulnerability, making Henry a preferred Week 8 option.

roster.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
roster.outlook: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to heal from an ankle injury in time for Detroit's Week 8 matchup versus Minnesota. St. Brown played a full game in Week 7 against the Packers, finishing with nine catches for a season-high 153 yards. The star pass catcher also tweaked his ankle in the game, and while he's not expected to miss any time, his situation is worth monitoring. St. Brown will aim to expand on a 46-525-5 receiving line opposite to a Vikings defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

roster.name: Rashee Rice
roster.outlook: Rashee Rice continues to work his way back from a hamstring strain, missing his second straight game in Kansas City's Week 7 loss to the Seahawks. Before getting injured in Week 4, Rice had produced an 11-171-0 line on 15 targets over the prior two games. Once he's cleared to return, he should immediately be Patrick Mahomes' top option in the passing game. If Rice does get back in the lineup in Week 8, he'll be facing a Broncos secondary that could once again be without Pat Surtain but still ranks sixth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Kyren Williams
roster.outlook: Kyren Williams will look to continue his consistent campaign when the Rams face the Chargers in Week 8. Williams posted 121 total yards Sunday against Las Vegas, marking the third time this season's he's logged over 100 total yards in a game. While his backfield mate Blake Corum has at times impacted Williams' workload, the latter has made the most of his carries, averaging a career-best 5.1 yards per rush, and he's also having his best season as a pass catcher. Williams could feast on a Chargers defense that's giving up 20.1 fantasy points per game to running backs to rank 25th in the league.

roster.name: Ladd McConkey
roster.outlook: Ladd McConkey has only missed one game so far in 2026, but injuries have marred the season for the Chargers' top wide receiver, and he comes out of the team's bye still in the league's concussion protocol. The offense as a whole has struggled, but McConkey's been productive when reasonably healthy, posting a 12-182-1 line on 15 targets over the first three weeks. If he's cleared to return in Week 8, he'll take on a stingy Rams secondary that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Patrick Mahomes
roster.outlook: Patrick Mahomes is coming off one of the worst performances of his career in Kansas City's Week 7 loss to the Seahawks. The two-time MVP threw for a season-low 165 yards with zero touchdowns and failed to get his team into the red zone for the first time in 153 career starts, including regular season and playoffs. With his wide receiver room thinned by injuries, Mahomes is again having a tough time stretching the field or taking advantage of a defense's focus on Kenneth Walker. He'll try to bounce back in Week 8 against a Broncos defense playing below expectations, which sits tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

roster.name: Tucker Kraft
roster.outlook: Tucker Kraft will look to build off a solid showing as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Kraft brought in four of six targets for 48 yards and his second touchdown of the season in Green Bay's Week 7 loss to the Lions. The featured tight end has now put up a 29-287-2 receiving line through the first seven games of the season. He'll face a Carolina defense that's ranked 20th in fantasy points allowed to TEs so far this campaign.

roster.name: Josh Downs
roster.outlook: Josh Downs has opened his fourth season in Indianapolis on a seven-game touchdown drought, and he has reached the 50-yard threshold just twice this season, with the last such performance coming in Week 3. It has been Keenan Allen rather than Downs stepping up during the continued absence of Alec Pierce (heel), who remains on injured reserve. Despite his disappointing production so far, Downs leads the Colts with 46 targets and is a decent flex option for Week 8 against a Jaguars defense that's allowing a league-high 210 receiving yards per game to WRs.

roster.name: Zach Charbonnet
roster.outlook: Zach Charbonnet (knee) has a chance to return to Seattle's backfield in Week 8 against Chicago. Charbonnet has yet to play since tearing his ACL in January, but he was activated off the reserve/PUP list last week and logged a trio of full practices. Though he ultimately didn't play Sunday against Kansas City, another week of practice could be enough for Charbonnet to make his return Monday against the Bears. Should that happen, he'll face a Chicago defense that has given up five total touchdowns (three rushing, two receiving) to running backs through seven games.

roster.name: Cam Little
roster.outlook: Cam Little has started 10-for-12 on field-goal attempts with a long of 60 across Jacksonville's first six games. The big-legged kicker could be in for a busy afternoon in Week 8 at home against the Colts, who are giving up 25.7 points per game and have allowed a league-high 21 field-goal attempts, 18 of which have been successful. Little is worth snagging off waivers if he was dropped during Jacksonville's Week 7 bye, as he profiles as a top-10 kicker for Week 8 and beyond.

roster.name: Harrison Butker
roster.outlook: Harrison Butker went just 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts in Kansas City's Week 7 loss to the Seahawks, the first time he's missed multiple attempts in a single game since 2018. The veteran kicker has missed five of 16 FG attempts overall this season, including one from inside 50 yards, and he may need to turn things around quickly to prevent KC from beginning a search for his replacement. Butker will try to bounce back in Week 8 against a Broncos team that's allowing 20.1 points a game, seventh in the league.

roster.name: DeMario Douglas
roster.outlook: DeMario Douglas will seek a rebound in Week 8 when New England travels to Miami. He was on a two-game heater entering Week 7, but finished with just three catches for 23 yards and has been held to 38 yards or fewer in five of seven outings. Miami is allowing an attractive 8.8 yards per target, the eighth-highest total league-wide, but because of vulnerabilities to tight ends and running backs in the passing game, opposing wideouts have the second-fewest yards, suggesting it may be better to look elsewhere for meaningful production.

roster.name: Justin Jefferson
roster.outlook: Justin Jefferson will look to get back in the end zone as the Vikings play the Lions in Week 8. Jefferson had a quiet performance out of the bye in Week 7, reeling in four of seven targets for 44 yards, which was his second-lowest yardage total of the year. The star wideout has now pieced together a 23-302-3 receiving line across five games this season. He'll have plenty of chances to carve up a Detroit secondary that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.

roster.name: Saquon Barkley
roster.outlook: Saquon Barkley returned from injury for the Eagles, only to tweak his hamstring while also suffering a compensatory back injury. Barkley rushed seven times for 62 yards and a touchdown, though played sparingly in the second half of the game, and ultimately could be sidelined again in Week 8 versus the Commanders. If Barkley is able to suit up, he will face a Washington defense that has been fairly stingy against the run in 2026.  The Commanders are allowing 100.5 rushing yards per clash, which is 14th in the league. In addition, Washington has allowed just five rushing touchdowns, which is tied for 11th in the league. If neither Barkley nor backup Dameon Pierce can play, Elijah Mitchell would be the only healthy option at running back.

roster.name: Josh Allen
roster.outlook: Josh Allen hopes to have his full complement of receivers when the Bills come out of their bye to host the Ravens in Week 8. He failed to record a rushing score in Week 6 for the first time all season, but threw multiple touchdowns for the first time since Week 2, maintaining his elite fantasy scoring. This game could bring shootout potential if Baltimore gets Lamar Jackson back under center. Baltimore's defense has been solid against opposing passers, allowing just five touchdown passes in six games before being solved by Joe Burrow for four in Week 7. They've also allowed just one rushing touchdown to the position, but Allen is matchup-proof.

roster.name: Quinshon Judkins
roster.outlook: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns are in Pittsburgh for an AFC North showdown in Week 8. He rushed 17 times for 96 yards and two touchdowns and caught his only target for eight yards during Cleveland's 27-24 victory in Week 7. Judkins returned from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury and posted his best performance of the year, setting season highs in rush yards and yards from scrimmage (104). He'll aim to stay hot against a Steelers defense allowing 20.5 fantasy points per game (T-11th) to RBs.

roster.name: Jameson Williams
roster.outlook: Jameson Williams will aim to keep it rolling as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Williams produced his best fantasy performance of the year in a Week 7 win over Green Bay, hauling in five of nine targets for 91 yards and two touchdowns. The speedy wideout has now produced four touchdowns in his last two games, along with seven catches for 138 yards in that stretch. He'll face a Minnesota defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
roster.outlook: Kyle Pitts will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Pitts has really found a rhythm over the last three weeks after a slow start to the season, catching 15 of 18 targets for 124 yards and four touchdowns over that span. Despite ranking fourth on the team in yards, Pitts has tallied the third-most targets (27) and the most touchdowns (four) on the Falcons through seven weeks. He's in for a favorable matchup as well, with the Buccaneers' defense giving up 16.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

roster.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
roster.outlook: Rhamondre Stevenson's role in the Patriots' passing game will keep him active in Week 8 against the Dolphins. While he is coming off his third single-digit carry game of the season, he's caught at least three passes in five games and five in two outings, an area where Miami's defense is particularly vulnerable. The Dolphins allow a moderate 4.3 yards per carry and just three rushing touchdowns to backs, yet have given up 34 catches, including five touchdown receptions, to running backs in six games. Stevenson has multiple paths to meaningful production.

roster.name: Sam LaPorta
roster.outlook: Sam LaPorta will aim to bounce back as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. LaPorta was silenced in a Week 7 win over the Packers, catching one of two targets for 18 yards. The starting tight end's performance will hopefully be an anomaly, and he still has a 28-334-3 receiving line through six outings this season. He'll face a Minnesota defense that's ranked a tough first in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Wan'Dale Robinson
roster.outlook: Wan'Dale Robinson mustered just seven yards on four catches in the Titans' Week 7 loss to the Browns, and he's likely to continue earning a steady diet of short passes from Cam Ward in Week 8 against the Bengals. Robinson has 23 catches over the past five games but is averaging a career-low 7.1 yards per reception in his fifth NFL season and first with Tennessee. He's a high-floor, low-ceiling flex option for Week 8 against the Bengals, who are allowing 138 yards per game to wide receivers.

roster.name: Denzel Boston
roster.outlook: Denzel Boston and the Browns head to Pittsburgh for an AFC North clash in Week 8. He hauled in three of eight targets for 27 yards in Cleveland's 27-24 victory in Week 7. Boston finished third on the team in targets but was a distant fourth in yardage behind fellow rookie KC Concepcion (129), Harold Fannin Jr. (91) and Dylan Sampson (32). Boston will look to rebound against a Steelers defense he posted a 4-89-0 receiving line on seven targets back in Week 4.

roster.name: Stefon Diggs
roster.outlook: Stefon Diggs will serve as the No. 1 wideout for the Commanders for the remainder of the season, as Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign due to a knee injury. Diggs has scored four times in five games played for Washington, following a return from a hamstring injury of his own. Following the bye, Washington will face division rival Philadelphia in Week 8. The reeling Eagles have been suspect in defending the pass this season.  Philadelphia is giving up 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.

roster.name: Aaron Rodgers
roster.outlook: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers welcome the division-rival Browns to town in Week 8. He completed 19 of 30 pass attempts for 212 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing three times for six yards during Pittsburgh's 16-10 win in Week 7. The performance snapped Rodgers' four-game multi-touchdown streak, although he was able to avoid making any turnovers. He'll aim to get back on track versus a Cleveland defense he threw for 299 yards and three TDs against during a Week 4 loss.

roster.name: Jordan Mason
roster.outlook: Jordan Mason could be in line for a workhorse role as the Vikings travel to Detroit in Week 8. Mason made his return from IR in Week 7 against the Colts and logged 15 carries for 68 yards, leading the ground game with Aaron Jones hurting his knee in the matchup. Jones' status is up in the air moving forward, so Mason's role could be even bigger if he has full command of the backfield. The Lions have ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

roster.name: James Cook III
roster.outlook: James Cook needs heavy volume in Week 8 to bolster Buffalo's offense against the Ravens. That hasn't been a problem, as he's amassed 20-plus touches in four of the Bills' first six outings, and he's continued scoring, finding the end zone in each of his last five games. Prior to a Week 7 bye, Cook had his best game as a receiver, possibly elevating his floor even higher. Baltimore is a stout defense against the run, allowing just 3.8 yards per carry, the eighth-lowest total in the league, but they have surrendered 86 yards or more to an opposing back three times. Barring an unexpected change in usage, Cook should be able to flirt with those numbers in Week 8.

roster.name: Omarion Hampton
roster.outlook: Omarion Hampton will look to turn his season around coming out of the Chargers' Week 7 bye. He failed to reach 50 scrimmage yards or get into the end zone in his last two games before the break, as Mike McDaniel turned his backfield into a committee. Hampton is the most talented back on the roster, but as long as Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal are garnering significant shares of the workload, all of them will have limited ceilings. Hampton will try to reassert himself as the No. 1 option in Week 8 against a Rams defense that's tied for 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Jeremiyah Love
roster.outlook: Jeremiyah Love has missed Arizona's past two games due to an ankle injury but could return in Week 8 against the Cowboys. Love is slated to practice this week, though that doesn't guarantee that he'll suit up versus Dallas. If the rookie running back misses another game, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight would likely continue to split the Cardinals' backfield work. Arizona's ground game could be set for a big day against a Dallas defense that is giving up 20.9 fantasy points per game to running backs, seventh-worst in the league.

roster.name: Emeka Egbuka
roster.outlook: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' top wideout if active for the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Egbuka was sidelined for the Week 7 win over the Panthers but still leads Tampa Bay in targets (49), receptions (28) and receiving touchdowns (two) this season. With Baker Mayfield at quarterback this year, Egbuka has averaged 4.3 receptions, 47 yards and 0.3 touchdowns per game. He could find success against a Falcons defense that's given up 34.4 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

roster.name: Jadarian Price
roster.outlook: Jadarian Price (chest) is eligible to return from IR for Seattle's Week 8 matchup against Chicago. Price hasn't played since Week 3, but he's expected to be designated to return this week. It remains to be seen if the rookie will be able to suit up against the Bears, and even if he does play, he may be part of a backfield committee that also includes Emanuel Wilson and the potentially returning Zach Charbonnet (knee). With that said, Seattle's backfield could find success against a Chicago defense that has given up 4.33 yards per carry to running backs, 25th in the league.

roster.name: Drake Maye
roster.outlook: Drake Maye's recent surge should continue when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. In Week 7, he topped 300 passing yards for the second time in three weeks and also added a rushing touchdown for the second time in three games, bringing his total to 14 touchdowns over his last four games. Miami's secondary has been decimated by opposing signal-callers, allowing seven touchdown passes in the last two weeks, multiple touchdown passes in five of six games, and the third-worst yards per attempt at 8.1. This firmly entrenches Maye in Week 8 lineups.

roster.name: Blake Corum
roster.outlook: Blake Corum is coming off his biggest workload of the campaign with the Rams' Week 8 matchup versus the Chargers on tap. After entering Sunday with fewer than 10 carries in four straight contests, Corum rumbled for 93 yards and a touchdown on a season-high 17 totes against the Raiders. Backfield mate Kyren Williams equaled Corum with 18 touches and figures to continue to lead the team's backfield, but Corum certainly reminded fantasy managers that he's worth consideration even in the No. 2 RB role. Both Corum and Williams could find room to run against a Chargers defense that ranks 21st in the league with 4.19 yards per carry allowed to running backs.

roster.name: KC Concepcion
roster.outlook: KC Concepcion and the Browns travel to Pittsburgh for a Week 8 divisional clash. He caught eight of 10 targets for 129 yards and had three carries for another 23 yards during Cleveland's comeback victory in Week 7. The rookie broke out with season highs in receptions, yardage and targets while leading the Browns in every category. Concepcion will aim to score his first touchdown of his career versus the Steelers 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (30.5) to WRs.

roster.name: Keenan Allen
roster.outlook: Keenan Allen is averaging over seven targets per game and has operated as the Colts' co-No. 1 WR alongside Josh Downs since Alec Pierce went down with a heel injury. Pierce remains on injured reserve ahead of a Week 8 trip to Jacksonville. Allen will be a high-floor flex candidate against a Jaguars defense that's giving up a league-high 210 yards per game to wide receivers. He's averaging 55 receiving yards per game over the past four and has scored one TD this season.

roster.name: Chad Ryland
roster.outlook: Chad Ryland has enjoyed a robust workload of late and could continue that trend in Arizona's Week 8 battle against Dallas. After attempting one or zero field goals in three of his first five games, Ryland has gone 9-for-9 in FG attempts over his past two contests. None of those tries have come from beyond 50 yards, but the volume has been a nice boon for his fantasy point production. Opposing kickers are 11-for-12 on FG tries against the Cowboys this season.

roster.name: Ryan Flournoy
roster.outlook: Ryan Flournoy was second on the Cowboys in receiving yards last game. Flournoy reeled in four passes for 70 yards in the 38-21 win over the Eagles. Flournoy has at least three catches in four-straight contests. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL. The Cardinals are also giving up 228 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL.

roster.name: Brenton Strange
roster.outlook: Brenton Strange has picked up the pace after a slow start and is a viable Week 8 starter at TE for Jacksonville's home game against the Colts. He has caught 19 of 23 targets for 207 yards over the past three games after being limited to seven catches for 72 yards on 10 targets through Week 3, though Strange hasn't scored since the season opener. Strange has a nice opportunity to snap his five-game touchdown drought against the Colts, who have allowed five TDs to TEs, which is tied for fifth-most in the NFL.

roster.name: Bijan Robinson
roster.outlook: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of Atlanta's offense during the Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Robinson has underwhelmed relative to his usual standards over the last two weeks, accounting for 175 total yards and no touchdowns on 36 touches. Despite the lack of scoring, Robinson has still managed to accumulate 4.3 yards per carry during that span. It will likely be tough for Robinson to have a bounce-back performance in Week 8 as well, with Tampa Bay's defense allowing just 18.2 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.

roster.name: Drake London
roster.outlook: Drake London is expected to remain one of fantasy's top wideouts in the Falcons' Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. London paced Atlanta's pass catchers in the Week 7 win over the 49ers, catching seven of nine targets for 66 yards and a score. Since quarterback Michael Penix returned from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London has averaged a whopping 6.4 receptions and 107.2 yards per game, making him one of the league's most productive WRs. He's in for a tough matchup in Week 8, however, as Tampa Bay's secondary has allowed just 29.6 fantasy points per game to the position this season.

roster.name: Tyler Warren
roster.outlook: Tyler Warren hasn't suited up since Week 5 due to a groin injury. He leads the Colts with 30 catches despite missing the past two games, so Warren would immediately return to the fantasy starting range if he gains clearance to return in Week 8 against a Jaguars defense that has been much more vulnerable through the air than on the ground. Jacksonville is holding TEs to 35 yards per game but has allowed the position to score four times in six outings, and Warren has accounted for three of the six TDs scored by Colts other than Jonathan Taylor.

roster.name: D'Andre Swift
roster.outlook: D'Andre Swift's role will be up in the air heading into Week 8 as the Bears travel to Seattle. Swift produced once again in Week 7, tallying 22 rushes for 78 yards and a touchdown, along with catching four passes for 12 yards. The veteran has benefited from a workhorse role with Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) out the last three weeks, finding the end zone four times and averaging over 19 touches per game in that stretch. Monangai could be in line to return this week, but the pair of running backs have proven to both hold value even when both active. Either way, Swift will face a Seahawks defense that's ranked top 10 in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs (15.4).

roster.name: DK Metcalf
roster.outlook: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Browns for a Week 8 showdown with first place in the AFC North on the line.
