He brought in two of six targets for 56 yards in Week 7 during Pittsburgh's 16-10 win in Paris. Metcalf tied for the lead in targets while pacing the team in yardage despite his low reception count. He'll be ready to face a Cleveland defense he cooked for a season-high 115 yards on five catches in Week 4.

roster.name: Rachaad White
roster.outlook: Rachaad White will serve as the No. 1 running back for the Commanders in Week 8, as starter Jacory Croskey-Merritt was placed on Injured Reserve with a groin injury. White has found the end zone in two of the last three games as a receiver out of the backfield, but is averaging just 4.0 yards per carry as a rusher. Still, the expanded role should give him double-digit touches against a floundering Eagles defense. Philadelphia is allowing 119.3 rushing yards per clash, which is 21st in the league.

roster.name: Jordan Addison
roster.outlook: Jordan Addison will aim to do more with his targets as the Vikings play the Lions in Week 8. Addison didn't do much again in Week 7 against the Colts, reeling in two of his three targets for 30 yards. The speedy pass catcher has put together an underwhelming start to the 2026 season, totaling just 13 catches for 183 yards and one touchdown across five games. He'll look to capitalize on a faulty Detroit defense that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Dalton Kincaid
roster.outlook: Dalton Kincaid hopes to rediscover some early season success with the Bills coming out of a bye week to host the Ravens in Week 8. After snagging 12 of 14 targets for 225 yards in his first two games, Kincaid has not topped 38 yards or scored in his subsequent four outings, despite maintaining a higher snap share than last season. Baltimore is allowing only 39.0 yards per game to opposing tight ends, setting up Kincaid for another quiet week, but the Ravens allowed two touchdowns to the position last week and five overall, potentially helping Kincaid break his scoring drought.

roster.name: Brian Robinson Jr.
roster.outlook: Brian Robinson (hamstring) will operate as Atlanta's No. 2 running back if active for the Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Robinson was sidelined for the Falcons' Week 7 win over the 49ers but has been a major part of the team's offense throughout the year. Despite playing behind Bijan Robinson, Brian Robinson has tallied 211 rushing yards, 30 receiving yards and four touchdowns in six contests. Even if he returns for the Week 8 divisional matchup, Robinson could struggle against a tough Buccaneers defense that's given up just 3.6 yards per carry this season.

roster.name: Jason Myers
roster.outlook: Jason Myers is in the midst of one of his most accurate NFL seasons going into Seattle's Week 8 matchup against Chicago. Myers has gone 14-for-15 on field-goal tries through seven games and is 16-for-17 on PAT attempts. He's made all three of his field-goal tries from 50-plus yards, with his only miss this season being a 47-yard attempt. However, the Bears haven't yielded many FG tries, allowing just 10 through seven weeks.

roster.name: T.J. Hockenson
roster.outlook: T.J. Hockenson remains a top option in Minnesota's passing game heading into Week 8 against the Lions. Hockenson found the end zone for the second time of the season in a Week 7 win over the Colts, and he complemented his score with four catches for 35 yards. The veteran tight end has now brought in 27 catches for 237 yards and two touchdowns this season. He enters a favorable matchup versus a Detroit defense that's ranked 32nd in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Jordan Love
roster.outlook: Jordan Love will aim to get the Packers back in the win column in Week 8 versus the Panthers. Even with Josh Jacobs back on the field at Detroit in Week 7, Green Bay still leaned on the passing game, with Love completing 27 of 45 passes for 274 yards with a 2:1 TD:INT ratio. He's now thrown for two touchdowns in all but one game this season, but he's still totaled two in every outing. Love should have no problem continuing his success against a Carolina defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy quarterbacks.

roster.name: Jonah Coleman
roster.outlook: Jonah Coleman had the biggest share of the backfield workload in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, handling 11 touches to J.K. Dobbins' six and RJ Harvey's five. Coleman's 69 scrimmage yards led the trio, but the other two each made trips to the end zone while the rookie RB was held out. It was still an impressive effort in his return from an IR stint due to an ankle injury, and Coleman might be the most likely player from the group to emerge as the lead back. A messy committee is the more probable arrangement, however, heading into a Week 8 clash with a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Jakobi Meyers
free_agents.outlook: Jakobi Meyers has established himself as the No. 2 WR for the Jaguars behind Parker Washington, putting Meyers firmly in the fantasy flex conversation for a Week 8 home game against the Colts. Meyers is averaging 48 receiving yards on 4.7 targets per game, and he set season highs in both of those categories with 83 yards on 10 targets in Jacksonville's Week 6 loss to the Texans prior to a Week 7 bye. The veteran wideout faced the Colts three times last season. Two of those meetings came after Meyers was acquired by the Jaguars in a midseason trade, and he mustered exactly 39 receiving yards in both games while scoring a touchdown in one of those matchups. He has five TDs in 15 regular-season games with Jacksonville.

free_agents.name: Kirk Cousins
free_agents.outlook: Kirk Cousins lost a fourth straight start in Week 7, but for now he'll remain the Raiders' starting quarterback ahead of rookie Fernando Mendoza. Cousins has cooled off against tougher competition, but he's still playing well and has a 7:2 TD:INT during the losing streak while averaging 304 passing yards a game. Brock Bowers and Tre Tucker remain his only reliable targets however, and Ashton Jeanty hasn't been able to force defenses to pay more attention to the team's ground game. Cousins may not need to air it out as much in Week 8 against a Jets defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

free_agents.name: Bo Nix
free_agents.outlook: Bo Nix contributed most with his legs in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, throwing one TD and running for another. The second score came in the second quarter on a 62-yard scamper, the longest rushing touchdown by a QB in an NFL regular-season game since 2022. Nix's 73 rushing yards on the day nearly doubled his total from the first six weeks combined. Despite that performance, Nix is still on pace for a career-worst campaign, and things won't get easier for him in Week 8 against a Kansas City defense that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

free_agents.name: Chris Godwin Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of Tampa Bay's top wideouts in the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Godwin was the Buccaneers' second-leading receiver in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, catching four of five targets for 27 yards. After Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was sidelined last week, Godwin now leads Tampa Bay in receiving yards (243) through seven games. Godwin could remain successful in Week 8 against a Falcons defense that's allowed 8.0 yards per target to opposing wideouts this season.

free_agents.name: Jake Ferguson
free_agents.outlook: Jake Ferguson was held without a catch last game for Dallas. Ferguson's decline has been steep this season. He has failed to find the end zone in four-straight games, and has not even gained 20 yards in any contest over that span. He will look to get back on track in Week 8 with an extremely favorable matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. Arizona has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Cameron Dicker
free_agents.outlook: Cameron Dicker failed to get an extra-point attempt in Week 6 for the first time this season, accounting for all the Chargers' points with two field goals in a 22-6 loss to Kansas City. Coming out of a bye, the offense will hopefully be a bit healthier and energized, providing Dicker with more opportunities, but he has kicked multiple field goals in three of the last four contests. In Week 8, he'll take aim at a Rams team that's allowing 22.7 points per game, 16th in the league.

free_agents.name: Justin Herbert
free_agents.outlook: Justin Herbert is hoping the Chargers' Week 7 bye will help the offense get sorted out. Through six games under offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and working behind a patchwork offensive line, the 28-year-old quarterback is on pace for career worst in every major category, including a 59.4% completion rate, 6.3 yards per attempt and a weak 5:8 TD:INT. He's even failed to score a rushing TD, after running for multiple scores in five of his first six NFL seasons. Herbert will try to right the ship in Week 8 against a Rams defense that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

free_agents.name: Sam Darnold
free_agents.outlook: Sam Darnold has thrown at least one pickoff in five straight games heading into Seattle's matchup against Chicago in Week 8. Darnold's eight total pickoffs are tied for most in the league despite the fact that he played only five snaps Week 1 and missed Week 2 altogether. The veteran quarterback hasn't recently been offsetting the interceptions with scores -- over his past three games, he's tossed just two total touchdowns. The Bears have given up 11 passing TDs this season, tied for eighth-most in the league, and have picked off just four passes, so perhaps Darnold can begin a turnaround.

free_agents.name: Keon Coleman
free_agents.outlook: Keon Coleman will try to extend his scoring streak to four games when Buffalo hosts the Ravens in Week 8. Despite his nose for the end zone, Coleman hasn't collected steady volume, three times being limited to just one catch, though more consistent opportunities have come with DJ Moore (shoulder) sidelined. Coming out of a bye, Moore likely is the healthiest he's been in some time, which may result in fewer snaps for Coleman. Should he remain involved, Baltimore has allowed three 100-yard games to outside receivers over the last four weeks, setting Coleman up for a potential productive outing.

free_agents.name: Travis Hunter
free_agents.outlook: Travis Hunter had his best offensive performance of the season in Week 6 against the Texans prior to Jacksonville's Week 7 bye, catching all four of his targets for 59 yards and a touchdown. He remains a full-time defensive player, but Hunter's offensive opportunities have increased in recent weeks. The former two-way college football star tied his season high with six snaps on offense in Week 5 against the Eagles before setting a new high with nine snaps against Houston in Week 6. Hunter is a risky fantasy option due to his limited opportunities, but he has the talent to make the most of his chances and is at least a viable dart throw in deeper formats in Week 8 against a Colts defense that's giving up 25.7 points per game.

free_agents.name: Rashid Shaheed
free_agents.outlook: Rashid Shaheed isn't certain to suit up for Seattle in Week 8 against the Bears. Shaheed injured his knee in Week 7 versus Kansas City, and though initial reports on the injury were promising, it's not clear if he'll need to miss time. The versatile wideout has been pretty quiet as a receiver throughout the campaign, surpassing three receptions just once through seven weeks. That makes him relatively dependent on big plays, and Chicago has given up nine receptions of 40-plus yards this season, most in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Baker Mayfield
free_agents.outlook: Baker Mayfield is expected to lead the Buccaneers' offense into the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Mayfield had a very light workload in his return from injury in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, completing seven of 11 pass attempts for 64 yards and a touchdown. In his first three games this season, Mayfield threw for an average of 205 yards, 0.7 touchdowns and 0.7 interceptions per contest. He'll look to catch fire against a Falcons defense that's given up 21.2 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

free_agents.name: Quentin Johnston
free_agents.outlook: Quentin Johnston has struggled this season along with the rest of the Chargers' offense, catching only one pass in three of his five games and failing to reach 60 receiving yards or score a TD in any of them. He has had receptions of 40-plus yards in each of his last two contests, however, reaffirming that he does have some big-play upside. Johnston faces a tough test in Week 8 against a Rams secondary that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Tyjae Spears
free_agents.outlook: Tyjae Spears has been banged up for most of the season. He sat out Tennessee's Week 7 loss to the Browns due to a knee injury after previously playing through ankle and knee injuries. He's a shifty change-of-pace option when healthy, but Spears won't be an advisable Week 8 fantasy play even if he suits up against the Bengals. Tony Pollard has strengthened his hold on the top spot on Tennessee's RB depth chart with strong play in recent weeks, and Spears is unlikely to score his first TD of the season against a Bengals defense that has allowed just three TDs to RBs through six games.

free_agents.name: Dameon Pierce
free_agents.outlook: Dameon Pierce still managed to maintain a solid role despite the return of Saquon Barkley from injury for the Eagles.  Barkley rushed seven times for 62 yards and a touchdown but tweaked his hamstring while also suffering a compensatory back injury. This allowed Pierce to take 14 carries for 47 yards and a touchdown of his own.  However, Pierce could be seen leaving the field late in the fourth quarter with a potential injury as well. If neither Barkley nor Pierce can play in Week 8 versus Washington, Elijah Mitchell would be the only healthy option at running back. The Commanders are allowing 100.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 14th in the league.

free_agents.name: Jacoby Brissett
free_agents.outlook: Jacoby Brissett will look to guide Arizona to more scoring in Week 8 versus Dallas. Though Brissett has thrown for a combined 490 yards over his past two games, he's tossed just one touchdown during that span. The veteran QB has taken to the air a league-high 282 times this season, so his fantasy managers have at least been able to count on consistent volume. Brissett could put up big numbers versus a Cowboys defense that ranks in the the bottom 10 of the league in fantasy points per game allowed to quarterbacks.

free_agents.name: Evan McPherson
free_agents.outlook: Evan McPherson and the Bengals return home for a Week 8 showdown against the 1-6 Titans. He did not attempt a field goal but converted all five of his extra-point tries during Cincinnati's 35-13 win in Week 7. McPherson is perfect through six contests this season, going 10-for-10 on FGs and 19-for-19 on PATs. However, with the Bengals offense routinely finding the endzone, his opportunities to make a big fantasy difference have suffered.

free_agents.name: Jayden Reed
free_agents.outlook: Jayden Reed will be inactive again as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, which requires season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Savion Williams and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.

free_agents.name: Michael Penix Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Michael Penix will continue leading the Falcons' offense into the Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Penix has rejuvenated Atlanta's offense since his return from injury, throwing for an average of 231.4 yards and 1.8 touchdowns per game. He has thrown for three touchdowns in consecutive games while turning the ball over just once, leading the Falcons to 30 points per game during that span. Despite this, Penix is in for a tough Week 8 matchup against a Buccaneers defense that's allowed just 18.5 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

free_agents.name: Mike Washington Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Mike Washington remains stuck as the backup to Ashton Jeanty in the Raiders' backfield, despite being more effective on the ground. Through seven games, Jeanty has a woeful 3.1 yards per carry on 106 totes, while Washington has produced 4.9 yards per carry on 40 rushes. Jeanty is the superior pass catcher, however, and coach Klint Kubiak has shown no signs of shifting the two closer to a timeshare. Washington will try to capitalize on his opportunities in Week 8 against a Jets defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Mike Gesicki
free_agents.outlook: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals host the 1-6 Titans in Week 8. He caught his only target for a six-yard touchdown during Cincinnati's 35-13 victory over Baltimore. Gesicki extended his TD streak to four consecutive games, as he's now compiled a 13-165-5 receiving line on 18 targets in 2026. He'll try to make it five in a row versus Tennessee's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per contest (11.1) to TEs.

free_agents.name: Kimani Vidal
free_agents.outlook: Kimani Vidal was seeing his usage increase prior to the Chargers' Week 7 bye, with the third-year running back handling a season-high 10 touches in a Week 6 loss to Kansas City, although he turned that volume into just 40 scrimmage yards and zero TDs. Omarion Hampton remains the back with the biggest upside on the roster, but Vidal and Keaton Mitchell are also in the mix, and Mike McDaniel may deploy a full-blown committee in his backfield as he searches for answers. Vidal will face a Rams defense in Week 8 that's tied for 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Samaje Perine
free_agents.outlook: Samaje Perine and the Bengals host the 1-6 Titans in Week 8. He had four carries for 16 yards and a one-yard touchdown but was not targeted during Cincinnati's Week 7 victory. The Bengals' backfield has been tricky with Chase Brown struggling as of late, and it looks like it could be headed toward more of a timeshare than initially thought at the start of the year. Perine will try to continue building momentum against the Titans' 19th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (22.3) to RBs.

free_agents.name: Deshaun Watson
free_agents.outlook: Deshaun Watson and the Browns travel to Pittsburgh for a divisional clash in Week 8. He completed 25 of 36 pass attempts for 308 yards with no touchdowns and one interception, while rushing three times for 19 yards and a TD during Cleveland's Week 7 victory. Watson mounted a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter for the fifth time this season, leading the Browns to a 5-2 record and a tie with the Steelers atop the AFC North. He'll face Pittsburgh's fourth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.1) to QBs for the second time in 2026. Watson threw for 268 yards with one TD and one INT to go along with 22 rush yards in a Week 4 win over the Steelers.

free_agents.name: Tyler Higbee
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Higbee continues to work in an unpredictable Rams tight-end timeshare ahead of a Week 8 matchup against the Chargers. While Matthew Stafford targeted tight ends 14 times in Sunday's win over Las Vegas, Higbee got just three of those looks and put up a meager 2-14-0 line. Meanwhile, fellow TEs Colby Parkinson (5-48-0) and Davis Allen (4-20-2) had bigger performances. Wideout Davante Adams (hamstring) is expected to miss several weeks, so Stafford will likely continue to look to his tight ends often, but it's anyone's guess which of the trio will be the top performer on a week-to-week basis. The Chargers have been relatively stingy against tight ends, giving up 6.8 fantasy points per game, tied for 10th in the league.

free_agents.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Chris Rodriguez remains No. 2 on Jacksonville's RB depth chart behind Bhayshul Tuten, limiting Rodriguez's Week 8 fantasy appeal to deeper formats. Rodriguez logged a season-high 11 carries in Jacksonville's Week 6 loss to the Texans prior to a Week 7 bye. He has handled fewer than six carries only once all season, but Rodriguez is a non-factor in the passing game, with just one catch in 2026. Rodriguez will be a touchdown-dependent fantasy play in Week 8 against a Colts defense that has allowed five rushing scores to RBs through seven games.

free_agents.name: Daniel Jones
free_agents.outlook: Daniel Jones has yet to generate a multi-touchdown performance this season for the Colts, and he threw for a season-low 108 yards in the Week 7 road loss to Minnesota. He'll face a Jaguars defense in Week 8 that's allowing the third-most passing yards per game but has limited QBs to a 7:7 TD:INT. Jones is below that mark with just a 4:7 TD:INT, so he'll be an unappealing fantasy option. Managers in deeper superflex and multi-QB formats can hope Jones records a decent passing yardage total against Jacksonville, though he is averaging a career-low 200 passing yards per game.

free_agents.name: Emmett Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Emmett Johnson continues to work his way into the Kansas City game plan as a pass-catcher. Over the last two games, the rookie has corralled four of six targets for 35 yards while the team deals with injuries to its wide receiver corps. Johnson will not challenge a healthy Kenneth Walker as the lead back, but Andy Reid is trying to find ways to get Johnson the ball in space. The result has been a 9-109-0 line on 11 targets through his first six NFL games. Johnson will look to score his first career touchdown in Week 8 against a Broncos defense that ranks 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Adonai Mitchell
free_agents.outlook: Adonai Mitchell has a minimal role in the Jets' limited passing attack entering a Week 8 clash with the Raiders. Returning from a four-week absence in Week 7, Mitchell failed to record a catch on his three targets. Omar Cooper's emergence paired with Garrett Wilson's steady presence won't leave a plethora of opportunities for the remaining Jets' receivers in a run-first offense, giving Mitchell too few chances to exploit a defense that's allowing a generous 8.9 yards per target through seven games.

free_agents.name: Mason Taylor
free_agents.outlook: Mason Taylor has an increasing role in the Jets' passing attack ahead of an inviting Week 8 matchup with the Raiders. Despite the presence of Kenyon Sadiq, Taylor's catch totals have increased in each of the last three games, spiking with a season-high five catches, 62 yards, and two touchdowns in Week 7. Las Vegas has been vulnerable to tight ends, allowing eight touchdowns in seven games; however, no one has topped 58 yards, setting Taylor up to be a bit touchdown-dependent.

free_agents.name: Dylan Sampson
free_agents.outlook: Dylan Sampson and the Browns travel to face the division-rival Steelers in Week 8. He rushed six times for 45 yards and caught all three targets for another 32 yards during Cleveland's Week 7 win. Sampson made his first appearance since Week 1 due to a knee injury that forced him to be placed on IR. Quinshon Judkins (ankle) also returned from a one-game absence and out-touched Sampson 18-9, but it was still encouraging for Sampson to take advantage of his opportunities. He'll look to build upon this showing versus a Steelers defense allowing 20.5 fantasy points per game (T-11th) to RBs.

free_agents.name: Roschon Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Roschon Johnson could return to a depth option as the Bears travel to Seattle in Week 8. Johnson benefited from the absence of Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) in Weeks 5 and 6, but he logged just two carries for 13 yards in Week 7 against the Patriots. With Monangai tracking for a possible return in the upcoming away matchup, Johnson's role is unlikely to hold much value. If Monangai does sit out again, Johnson's worth keeping an eye on even versus a Seahawks defense that's ranked top 10 in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs (15.4).

free_agents.name: Rashod Bateman
free_agents.outlook: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 8 clash against the Bills. He hauled in two of four targets for 33 yards during Baltimore's 35-13 loss in Week 7. Tyler Huntley attempted 34 passes and connected with eight different receivers on the day, but Zay Flowers (8-137-1) was the only one with more than three receptions and five targets. Lamar Jackson (ankle) could return from a three-game absence in Week 8, so Bateman may have an opportunity to take advantage of a Bills defense allowing the most fantasy points per game (42.3) to WRs.

free_agents.name: Ryan Fitzgerald
free_agents.outlook: Ryan Fitzgerald will likely have limited scoring opportunities in the Panthers' Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Fitzgerald made just one of two point-after tries in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers and has now missed five this season. Despite going 11 for 11 on field-goal attempts, Fitzgerald has converted on a league-low 70.6% of his extra points. He likely won't have many scoring chances against Green Bay either, as the Packers defense has allowed just 4.7 kicking points per game this season, the fewest in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Malik Willis
free_agents.outlook: Malik Willis needs his legs to create a fantasy-relevant outing in Week 8 when the Dolphins face the Patriots. He has rushed for a touchdown in consecutive games and has at least eight carries in three of four contests, while also coming off his first multi-touchdown passing effort of the season. New England has only allowed nine touchdown passes and 70 total rushing yards to quarterbacks, suggesting Willis faces an uphill battle for counting stats. However, game flow could force additional passing volume assuming Miami falls behind early, creating a path to fantasy production.

free_agents.name: Darren Waller
free_agents.outlook: Darren Waller is expected to remain Carolina's top receiving option at tight end in the Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Despite the Panthers' poor offensive performance in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, Waller was productive, catching one of two targets for 50 yards and a touchdown. On the season, Waller has paced Carolina's tight-end corps in touchdowns (three), targets (22) and yards (198). However, he could struggle against a strong Packers defense in Week 8 that's allowed just 9.0 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs this season, the second-fewest in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Cooper Kupp
free_agents.outlook: Cooper Kupp may be operating without fellow wideout Rashid Shaheed during Seattle's Week 8 matchup versus Chicago. Shaheed suffered a knee injury Sunday against Kansas City and is a question mark to play versus the Bears. If he does miss Week 8, Kupp could be set for more responsibilities, though he'd still be far behind superstar Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the pecking order. The Bears rank in the middle of the pack with 20.1 fantasy points per game allowed to wide receivers.

free_agents.name: Justice Hill
free_agents.outlook: Justice Hill and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 8 meeting with the Bills. He had three carries for seven yards and caught three of four targets for 26 yards during Baltimore's 35-13 loss in Week 7. Rasheen Ali registered 19 yards on four carries, but that can likely be attributed to the Ravens giving up all 35 points in the second half. Regardless, as long as Derrick Henry is healthy, Hill's involvement on offense will continue to be limited.

free_agents.name: Treylon Burks
free_agents.outlook: Treylon Burks could see an uptick in targets for the remainder of the season, as No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign for the Commanders due to a knee injury. Burks posted season highs in targets, receptions and receiving yardage in Washington's last game before the bye.  In Week 8, Washington will face division rival Philadelphia. The reeling Eagles have been suspect in defending the pass this season.  Philadelphia is giving up 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.

free_agents.name: Colby Parkinson
free_agents.outlook: Colby Parkinson could play a key role for the Rams in Week 8 against the Chargers. With wideout Davante Adams sidelined by a hamstring injury this past Sunday, QB Matthew Stafford targeted tight ends 14 times. Parkinson logged six of those looks, turning them into a 5-48-0 line. Adams is expected to be out multiple more weeks, so Parkinson and the Rams' other tight ends should continue to be looked to often. The Chargers rank 10th in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends thanks largely to giving up only one touchdown to the position so far.

free_agents.name: Kendrick Bourne
free_agents.outlook: Kendrick Bourne could be primed for a bounce-back performance when Arizona travels to Dallas in Week 8. Bourne was quiet against Denver this past Sunday, logging just three catches for nine yards. However, he tied for third on the team with six targets as he continues to get a decent amount of looks behind top wideout Michael Wilson and star tight end Trey McBride. Bourne has an appealing matchup against the Cowboys, who are giving up 163.1 receiving yards per game to wideouts to rank 25th in the league in that category.

free_agents.name: Jake Elliott
free_agents.outlook: Jake Elliott has not even attempted a field goal over the last two games for the Eagles. With Tanner McKee taking over the offense for Jalen Hurts, the offense has continued to sputter. The Eagles have scored 21 points or fewer in every contest during the current five-game losing streak.  In fact, Elliott has only attempted five field goals on the entire season. If the Eagles cannot put up points against an extremely suspect Washington defense in Week 8, Elliott's utility may have come to an end. The Commanders are allowing 28.7 points per game in 2026, which is second-to-last in the league.

free_agents.name: Calvin Ridley
free_agents.outlook: Calvin Ridley (hip) sat out for the Titans in Week 7 against the Browns. Even if he returns for Week 8 against the Bengals, Ridley won't be a viable fantasy option. He has caught a pass in only three of six appearances this season, with season totals of five catches for 81 yards while operating in a depth role at WR.

free_agents.name: Nick Folk
free_agents.outlook: Nick Folk will likely have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Falcons' Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Folk went five-for-six on kicks during the Week 7 win over the 49ers, making all three field goals but just two of three extra points. On the season, the veteran kicker has converted on 12 of 15 field-goal attempts and 15 of 16 point-after tries. He's in for a favorable Week 8 matchup against a Buccaneers defense that's allowed 8.7 kicking points per game this season.

free_agents.name: Ted Hurst III
free_agents.outlook: Ted Hurst is expected to operate as one of the Buccaneers' top wideouts during the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Despite a larger offensive role without Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) in Week 7, Hurst was quiet, failing to catch his lone target. The rookie wideout has now been held without a reception in two of his last three games, suggesting Tez Johnson's return could limit Hurst's fantasy value going forward. Despite this, Hurst could find value against a Falcons defense that's given up 6.3 yards per pass attempt this season.

free_agents.name: Wil Lutz
free_agents.outlook: Wil Lutz was busy and efficient in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, converting all three of his extra points and all three of his field-goal attempts for a season-best 12 points. The veteran kicker has booted multiple FGs in three of the last four games and multiple PATs in three straight, but the overall struggles of the Denver offense put a cap on Lutz's upside. He likely won't be able to squander any opportunities in Week 8 against a Kansas City team that ranks second in the NFL in points per game allowed.

free_agents.name: Darnell Washington
free_agents.outlook: Darnell Washington and the Steelers host the Browns for a divisional clash in Week 8. He caught his only target for a four-yard touchdown in Week 7 during Pittsburgh's 16-10 victory in Paris. Washington has a TD in two straight contests and three of his last four, as he now has a 16-160-3 line on 23 targets across seven games. He remains a touchdown-or-bust play in fantasy, although his first score of the season came against Cleveland during their first matchup in Week 4.

free_agents.name: Tanner McKee
free_agents.outlook: Tanner McKee was mediocre last game for the Eagles. McKee completed 23-of-35 passes for 211 yards, one touchdown and one interception in the 38-21 loss to Dallas. McKee has thrown for at least 210 yards and a touchdown in each of his starts for Philadelphia. In Week 8, he will face a Commanders defense that has been rather poor in defending the pass in 2026. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.

free_agents.name: Pierre Strong Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Pierre Strong will likely be a depth option again as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. The return of Josh Jacobs in Week 7 against the Lions knocked Strong down a peg, and he did not log a touch, with MarShawn Lloyd assuming the secondary running back role. Strong could remain a passing-down option with Chris Brooks out another week on IR, but his role moving forward still remains in jeopardy. Carolina has ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Cam Ward
free_agents.outlook: Cam Ward has yet to throw multiple touchdown passes in a game heading into the Titans' Week 8 trip to Cincinnati. The second-year QB has an ugly 4:5 TD:INT while throwing for just 168 yards per game. Cincinnati's defense has limited QBs to a 6:4 TD:INT, but the Bengals allowed Baltimore's Tyler Huntley to throw for a career-high 298 yards in a Week 7 game that the Bengals won by 22 points. Until Ward shows signs of progress as a passer, he'll remain a fantasy non-factor, even in superflex formats.

free_agents.name: Konata Mumpfield
free_agents.outlook: Konata Mumpfield is an option to fill a massive void in the Rams' receiver corps in Week 8 against the Chargers. With Davante Adams sidelined for several games due to a hamstring injury, the Rams are looking for someone to step up alongside star wideout Puka Nacua. That didn't happen in Week 7 -- aside from Nacua, the only one of the team's WRs to log a catch was Mumpfield, who finished with just one reception for 15 yards on two targets. Perhaps Mumpfield can make a big play or two against the Chargers, who rank 24th in the league by allowing 8.86 yards per target to wideouts.

free_agents.name: Jalen Nailor
free_agents.outlook: Jalen Nailor cannot seem to get on the same page as Kirk Cousins. Despite a consistent snap share due to his blocking skills, Nailor has caught just three of nine targets for 23 yards in two games since returning from a concussion. Brock Bowers, Tre Tucker and Ashton Jeanty are the only players getting regular looks from Cousins, but Nailor isn't doing much with the small volume he does see, and he might be looking forward to the day when rookie Fernando Mendoza takes over the offense. Nailor will try to make a splash in Week 8 against a Jets secondary that is tied for 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Jaylen Wright
free_agents.outlook: Jaylen Wright has not played a meaningful role out of the Dolphins' backfield and is uncertain to play in Week 8 against the Patriots due to a quad issue. He had five or six carries in each of his last three games, failing to average better than 1.8 yards per carry, and has not caught a pass all season. Facing a middling New England run defense seems less important than considering Wright's continued lack of clean health and the potential that Miami falls behind early and abandons the run.

free_agents.name: Elijah Mitchell
free_agents.outlook: Elijah Mitchell could end up seeing significant carries in Week 8 for the Eagles due to injury.  Both Saquon Barkley and Dameon Pierce appeared to leave the last game early due to various ailments, leaving Mitchell as potentially the only healthy back for the upcoming matchup with Washington.  Will Shipley and Tank Bigsby are already on Injured Reserve. If Mitchell maintains a role, he will face a Commanders defense allowing 100.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 14th in the league.

free_agents.name: Jason Sanders
free_agents.outlook: Jason Sanders hasn't been a high-scoring option in the Jets' limited offense ahead of a Week 8 matchup with the Raiders. Through seven games, Sanders has only 10 PATs while making one or two field goals in five of those outings. The Raiders are allowing the 10th-fewest fantasy points to kickers, as opponents routinely convert drives into touchdowns (24 PATs, just 10 field goal attempts). There are likely safer kickers available for Week 8 fantasy production.

free_agents.name: Cade Otton
free_agents.outlook: Cade Otton is expected to remain one of Baker Mayfield's top targets in the Buccaneers' Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Otton went without a catch during Tampa Bay's Week 7 win over the Panthers. However, this was largely due to the Buccaneers' success on the ground, as quarterback Baker Mayfield threw for just 64 yards while the team accumulated 258 rushing yards. Otton will have a good bounce-back opportunity against a Falcons defense that's allowed 16.4 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

free_agents.name: Jahan Dotson
free_agents.outlook: Jahan Dotson is expected to operate as one of Atlanta's top receiving options in the Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Dotson had a quiet day in the Week 7 win over the 49ers, catching just one of three targets for six yards. However, he had already emerged as the Falcons' No. 2 wideout prior to Sunday's win, catching seven of 12 targets for 195 yards and two touchdowns from Weeks 4 through 6. Dotson will look to get back on track against a solid Buccaneers defense in Week 8 that's given up just 7.2 yards per target on the season.

free_agents.name: Tyler Huntley
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Huntley and the Ravens travel to battle the Bills in Week 8. He threw for a career-high 298 yards (23-for-34) with one TD and one INT while rushing three times for 12 yards during Baltimore's Week 7 loss. Lamar Jackson (ankle) is expected to make his return following a three-game absence, which would return Huntley to the backup role. If Jackson is unable to suit up against the Bills' 30th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (26.5) to QBs, Huntley would earn his fourth consecutive start under center and be a streaming candidate.

free_agents.name: Tez Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Tez Johnson is expected to play a depth role in the Buccaneers' receiving corps in the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Johnson has operated as Tampa Bay's top deep threat over the last three weeks, catching five of six targets for 104 yards and a touchdown. Due to his lack of opportunities, he's unlikely to be fantasy relevant without scoring a touchdown. However, he could find the end zone against a Falcons defense that's allowed four receiving touchdowns to WRs this season.

free_agents.name: Jauan Jennings
free_agents.outlook: Jauan Jennings will seek to build on a season-best performance as the Vikings take on the Lions in Week 8. Jennings had a quiet start to the season heading into Minnesota's bye, logging just two catches for nine yards off five targets in four games. The veteran wide receiver turned it around in Week 7 against the Colts, though, hauling in two of three targets for 34 yards. Jennings should still be a secondary look moving forward, but he'll look to continue to carve out targets versus a Detroit defense that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Chris Brooks
free_agents.outlook: Chris Brooks will be out again in Week 8 as the Packers take on Carolina. Brooks is currently on IR with an ankle injury, which will keep him out for at least the next week. His absence from the field could continue to give Pierre Strong more opportunities, but the return of Josh Jacobs has shaken up the RB room. Brooks' next chance to see the field will be in Week 9 against the Patriots.

free_agents.name: Tre' Harris
free_agents.outlook: Tre' Harris missed the Chargers' last game before a bye due to a hamstring injury, but the time off could allow him to return to the lineup. The bigger issue for the second-year wideout is the state of the offense around him, as he's topped 60 receiving yards only once in five games and is still looking for his first touchdown of 2026. Ladd McConkey could also return from an injury in Week 8, which might leave Harris struggling to get significant volume against a stingy Rams secondary that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Ty Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Ty Johnson continues to produce when asked, but his role remains limited as the Bills get set to face the Ravens in Week 8. Used almost exclusively in the passing game, Johnson has 12 catches over four games since returning to health, averaging a decent 12.9 yards per catch. The volume remains too small to trust, and the Ravens have allowed just 102 yards and 2.6 yards per target to opposing running backs in the passing game, further dampening Johnson's potential.

free_agents.name: Dohnte Meyers
free_agents.outlook: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals are at home in Week 8 to square off against Tennessee. He failed to catch either of his two targets in Cincinnati's 35-13 victory in Week 7. Meyers was unable to take advantage of Joe Burrow's productive day, as he threw for 292 yards and four TDs. Meyers should remain on fantasy benches, with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins occupying a massive target share despite a solid matchup versus the Titans.

free_agents.name: Efton Chism III
free_agents.outlook: Efton Chism will hope to be more than an afterthought in the Patriots' passing game in Week 8 against the Dolphins. After showing some potential with A.J. Brown sidelined, Chism has just two targets over the last two weeks, resulting in a 16-yard catch. New England heavily targeted tight ends in Week 7, and that appears to be an effective strategy against Miami as well, likely limiting opportunities for Chism to post high catch or yardage totals.

free_agents.name: Evan Engram
free_agents.outlook: Evan Engram remains an afterthought in the Broncos' offense. He's caught two or fewer passes for under 20 yards in five of seven games this season, and his only touchdown came back in Week 1. Denver's passing game in general has been stagnant, leaving little volume for secondary options like Engram. However, he could be in position to break out in Week 8 against a Kansas City defense that's been stingy against other positions but ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

free_agents.name: Isaac TeSlaa
free_agents.outlook: Isaac TeSlaa will seek to stay involved as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. After a promising stretch from Weeks 2-5, TeSlaa has now recorded just one catch for 10 yards off four targets in his last two games. The young pass catcher will aim to get back to relevance against a Minnesota defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

free_agents.name: Andre Szmyt
free_agents.outlook: Andre Szmyt and the Browns travel to Pittsburgh for an AFC North showdown in Week 8. He went 2-for-3 on field goals and made all three of his PATs during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 7. Szmyt nailed the game-winning 32-yard field goal as time expired, making up for the 43-yarder he missed earlier in the fourth quarter. He's now made at least two FGs in six straight contests and drilled game-winners in consecutive games. Szmyt will try to keep up the momentum versus a Steelers defense allowing just 19.7 points per game, the fifth-lowest mark in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Gunnar Helm
free_agents.outlook: Gunnar Helm has an inkling of fantasy value in deeper formats thanks to a favorable Week 8 matchup, though his lack of production suggests Tennessee's starting TE may not make the most of this opportunity. He has yet to exceed 28 receiving yards in a game or score a TD all season, but perhaps Helm can improve the yardage metric in Week 8 against a Bengals defense that's allowing 85 receiving yards per game to TEs, which is second-most in the NFL. Cincinnati has yet to allow a TD to the position, though.

free_agents.name: Austin Ekeler
free_agents.outlook: Austin Ekeler managed just three touches for seven yards last game for Washington. Even with starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt on Injured Reserve with a groin injury, Ekeler was on the field for just seven of 67 offensive snaps. Rachaad White should get the start in Week 8 versus the Eagles, and Jeremy McNichols may see more work than Ekeler between the tackles. McNichols had five carries for 13 yards in his return from injury. Whomever gets touches does have a favorable matchup, as Philadelphia is giving up 119.3 yards per clash on the ground, which is 21st in the league.

free_agents.name: Oronde Gadsden
free_agents.outlook: Oronde Gadsden continues to struggle to earn a consistent role in Mike McDaniel's offense due to his lack of blocking skills. Gadsden's one of the few Charger skill players who has yet to miss a game this season, but he's still managed just a 12-103-1 line on 21 targets through six games, and he's fallen behind Charlie Kolar on the depth chart. Gadsden seems unlikely to turn though around in Week 8 against a stingy Rams defense that's tied for third in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

free_agents.name: Andy Borregales
free_agents.outlook: Andy Borregales has been more of a victim than a benefactor of the Patriots' surging offense ahead of a Week 8 matchup against the Dolphins. With Drake Maye putting New England into the end zone with great frequency over the last four weeks, Borregales has made 14 PATs but has attempted just four field goals in that stretch. That script seems likely to manifest again in Week 8 against a Miami defense that's allowed just 12 field goal tries in six games, but 17 extra points, creating a low but stable floor with less upside for Borregales.

free_agents.name: Chris Bell
free_agents.outlook: Chris Bell hasn't been able to stretch the field for the Dolphins as they enter a Week 8 matchup with the Patriots. He has been held without a catch in three of his first six games and has just eight catches during his rookie season in Miami's low-volume passing game, which isn't sustaining even one viable receiver, let alone multiple. While Miami will likely have to throw as this game progresses and the matchup is favorable with New England allowing 8.8 yards per target, Bell lacks the track record to be in the Week 8 mix.

free_agents.name: Savion Williams
free_agents.outlook: Savion Williams should continue to stay involved as the Packers play Carolina in Week 8. Williams has been consistently used since he returned from IR in Week 6, logging seven catches for 79 yards and four carries for 13 yards in the last two weeks. The second-year playmaker is still positioned behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden in the WR room, but he's been getting plenty of touches in a de facto Jayden Reed role. Williams will face a Panthers defense that's ranked fifth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

free_agents.name: Eli Raridon
free_agents.outlook: Eli Raridon could be a sneaky option when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. Since not playing in Week 3, Raridon has garnered 14 targets over the last four games, turning them into 10 catches and a touchdown. While the volume isn't elite and New England continues to spread passing work across a plethora of options, Miami has been very vulnerable to opposing tight ends, allowing six touchdowns in as many weeks and the second-highest yards per target at 9.3, suggesting Raridon could pop with minimal opportunities.

free_agents.name: Zachariah Branch
free_agents.outlook: Zachariah Branch is expected to play a depth role in the Falcons' receiving corps during the Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Branch played a career-high 37% of the Falcons' offensive snaps in the Week 7 win over the 49ers. Despite this, he logged just two touches for 17 yards and will likely remain irrelevant for fantasy purposes without finding the end zone. That could be difficult against a strong Tampa Bay secondary that's given up just five receiving touchdowns to WRs all season.

free_agents.name: Greg Dulcich
free_agents.outlook: Greg Dulcich has an uphill battle to maintain his ascending role in the Dolphins' passing game during a Week 8 matchup with the Patriots. He collected at least five targets in three of his last four games and is coming off a season-high 86 yards in Week 7, but New England has defended tight ends well, surrendering just 6.7 yards per target and two touchdowns. Game flow will likely favor Dulcich with the Patriots expected to jump out to a lead, though Dulcich lacking a touchdown reception tempers optimism.

free_agents.name: KaVontae Turpin
free_agents.outlook: KaVontae Turpin did not suit up last game for the Cowboys due to a rib injury.  Turpin has been more of an ancillary part of the offense even when healthy, as he has just four catches and two carries on the season. CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy handle most of the targets from quarterback Dak Prescott.  However, if Turpin somehow can suit up, he could have a favorable matchup if targeted. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Drew Stevens
free_agents.outlook: Drew Stevens has made at least two field goals in four of six games this season for Washington. However, he has made just 10 field goals the entire year overall, while missing three extra points. In Week 8, the Commanders face the Eagles. Philadelphia is allowing 22.8 points per contest, which is 17th in the league.

free_agents.name: Kyle Williams
free_agents.outlook: Kyle Williams will likely remain a low-volume, field-stretching option for the Patriots in Week 8 against the Dolphins. Williams has only two targets over the last two weeks with A.J. Brown back to full health. Miami is vulnerable against the pass, but has been exploited by tight ends and running backs more than receivers, a recipe New England cooked up in Week 7 and seems probable to follow again in Week 8. This leaves Williams with far too few chances to exploit a secondary that's allowing 8.8 yards per target to opposing receivers.

free_agents.name: Sione Vaki
free_agents.outlook: Sione Vaki should remain a low-usage second option as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Vaki was on the field for a season-low 12 percent of offensive snaps against the Packers in Week 7, and he logged just one carry for five yards. While the third-year running back is still the main option behind Jahmyr Gibbs at this point in the season, that role has proven to be minuscule. Vaki will also have to face a Minnesota defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to RBs for the snaps that he is on the field.

free_agents.name: Marvin Mims Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Marvin Mims is coming off his best performance of the season, catching both his targets for 53 yards, gaining three yards on his only carry, and adding 111 kick return yards. While the production on offense was modest, Mims has been the wide receiver to benefit most from the absence of Pat Bryant in the Broncos' underpowered passing game. Bryant will miss at least one more game with an ankle injury, but Mims will struggle to take advantage in Week 8 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Myles Price
free_agents.outlook: Myles Price remains a depth option heading into Minnesota's Week 8 matchup at Detroit. Price didn't log a full game in Week 7 against the Colts as he was being evaluated for a concussion, and this translated to zero targets. The sophomore remains a return guru at this point in the season, but it remains to be seen if his five catches for 26 yards across Weeks 4 and 5 before Minnesota's bye were a fluke. He'll face a Lions defense that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Jalen Royals
free_agents.outlook: Jalen Royals has yet to earn the trust of Patrick Mahomes. The second-year wide receiver has notched multiple targets in three straight games as part of an injury-depleted Kansas City wide receiver group, but he's managed a mere 2-24-0 line on eight total targets. Royals' struggles could put additional pressure on the team to trade for an established wideout before the deadline, as Rashee Rice has been the only consistent option at the position, and he's struggled to stay healthy. Royals will try to contribute in Week 8 against a Broncos secondary that ranks sixth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
